one_line_idea: Claimed viewpoint invariance of self-supervised ViT features collapses at a measurable camera-baseline knee, and the knee position, not average similarity, predicts a backbone's 3D utility.
core_hypothesis: Feature view-invariance is mostly co-visible texture matching and decays nonlinearly with viewpoint change: there is a baseline angle beyond which correspondence utility drops toward chance while narrow-baseline metrics stay high.

one_line_idea: Geometric information in vision foundation models peaks in middle transformer blocks, so standard last-layer feature extraction systematically understates and misranks the 3D awareness of 2D backbones.
core_hypothesis: Depth, surface-normal, and correspondence information is concentrated in middle blocks and is progressively discarded by later blocks that specialize toward semantic abstraction, and the peak layer shifts with pretraining objective.

one_line_idea: Learned feature upsamplers make features look sharper while corrupting the sub-pixel geometric signal, so pipelines that match or triangulate upsampled features get worse 3D estimates than bilinear baselines.
core_hypothesis: Upsamplers trained with image-guided objectives snap feature boundaries to intensity edges, which hallucinates spatial precision: the apparent localization is inherited from the guidance image, not the feature content, and it biases correspondence residuals near depth discontinuities.

one_line_idea: Image-text contrastive features are not geometry-poor: controlling for resolution and probe capacity, their coarse depth-ordering knowledge matches self-supervised features, and the reported gap is a protocol artifact.
core_hypothesis: Much of the measured 3D-awareness gap between image-text and self-distilled backbones is explained by input resolution and effective patch density rather than the pretraining objective.

one_line_idea: Foundation features carry a systematic metric-scale bias inherited from the crop-scale distribution of pretraining augmentations, measurable as a predictable error in apparent-size judgments.
core_hypothesis: Frozen features encode apparent object scale with a bias toward the pretraining crop-scale distribution: probes estimating physical size or distance will show errors correlated with the mismatch between test-time object scale and the augmentation scale density.

one_line_idea: Under controlled synthetic viewpoint sweeps, generative-diffusion features are not more multi-view consistent than contrastive features once texture density is controlled, contradicting a growing assumption in 3D distillation work.
core_hypothesis: Apparent cross-view stability advantages of diffusion features come from their sensitivity to low-frequency appearance, which correlates across views for texture-poor content, not from superior geometric encoding.

one_line_idea: A measurable fraction of reported 3D awareness in ViT probes is absolute positional-embedding leakage: probes read where a patch is in the frame, not what geometry the features encode.
core_hypothesis: A nontrivial share of probe performance survives feature ablation but not position ablation, meaning current 3D-awareness numbers overstate the geometry actually encoded in appearance features.

one_line_idea: Textureless-surface correspondence failure of foundation features is a token-granularity artifact, and dense overlapping-stride re-extraction recovers most of it without any retraining.
core_hypothesis: Much of the failure is quantization: coarse patch grids average away weak shading gradients that do carry correspondence signal, so densely re-extracting features with overlapping strides and aggregating them recovers usable matches on low-texture regions.

one_line_idea: Decomposing 2D features into view-invariant and view-dependent components before lifting them into 3D feature fields yields more geometrically faithful fields than the standard practice of averaging raw features across views.
core_hypothesis: A per-scene low-rank decomposition separating features into a view-independent term plus a small view-conditioned residual will reduce cross-view inconsistency of the lifted field and improve geometry-sensitive downstream readouts without new pretraining.

one_line_idea: Jointly distilling 2D semantic features into Gaussian-splat scenes measurably degrades the recovered geometry relative to photometric-only optimization, a cost the feature-field literature does not report.
core_hypothesis: Feature-rendering losses reward placing primitives where 2D features are stable rather than where surfaces are, systematically biasing Gaussian positions and opacities and worsening depth and surface accuracy versus photometric-only baselines.

one_line_idea: Foundation features cannot disambiguate the front and back of near-symmetric objects, and the error direction is predicted by canonical-pose frequency in web imagery, making pose pipelines built on them systematically biased rather than randomly wrong.
core_hypothesis: For objects with approximate front-back symmetry, feature matching resolves the ambiguity by defaulting to the pose most frequent in web photos, producing structured 180-degree errors whose frequency tracks canonical-pose bias rather than image evidence.

one_line_idea: The believed semantics-versus-geometry fine-tuning tradeoff in foundation backbones is a protocol artifact: tuning only late blocks at small learning rates buys large geometry gains at near-zero semantic cost.
core_hypothesis: The reported tradeoff comes from full-network tuning at semantic-task learning rates; geometry-relevant capacity is concentrated in late blocks whose careful tuning improves depth and correspondence probes while leaving semantic retrieval essentially intact.

one_line_idea: Monocular depth foundation models infer focal length implicitly from image content, and their metric-depth errors are largely explained by the error of that hidden focal estimate.
core_hypothesis: These models contain an implicit focal-length estimator driven by content cues (face sizes, room proportions, edge convergence), and metric-depth error decomposes into a dominant multiplicative term tracking hidden focal error plus a smaller residual.

master_adjacent: J-011 (photometric/lens prior boundary of repurposed generators)

one_line_idea: Generalization of monocular depth models scales with scene-layout diversity of training data, not raw image count, and layout-diversity-matched subsets can replicate full-data performance at a fraction of the size.
core_hypothesis: Cross-domain depth error is governed by coverage of scene-layout statistics (depth-range distribution, openness, clutter) rather than image count; beyond layout coverage saturation, additional images yield negligible gains.

one_line_idea: Teacher-student pseudo-label distillation, the engine of current depth foundation models, systematically erodes depth discontinuities with each generation, measurable as monotonic depth-edge degradation across distillation rounds.
core_hypothesis: Averaging effects in teacher ensembling and student regression act as an edge low-pass filter: each distillation generation smooths depth discontinuities further, degrading edge localization while global AbsRel improves or holds.

one_line_idea: Ordinal errors of relative-depth models concentrate at object-ground contact ambiguities, so a contact-focused probe set exposes large headroom that whole-image ranking metrics hide.
core_hypothesis: Remaining ordinal errors are not uniformly distributed but concentrate at pixel pairs spanning object-ground contact and support boundaries, where pictorial cues are ambiguous; aggregate ordinal metrics dilute these decisive pairs.

one_line_idea: Detected object instances of known physical size classes act as an implicit calibration rig: a post-hoc scale solver over class-size priors converts relative depth to metric depth competitively with intrinsics-aware models on populated scenes.
core_hypothesis: For scenes containing common object classes, a robust joint solve over class-size distributions and a global scale-shift transform yields metric depth whose accuracy approaches intrinsics-conditioned models, because size priors over multiple instances over-constrain the scale.

one_line_idea: Depth foundation models fail on non-pinhole imagery with a characteristic radial error signature, and a lens-conditioned resampling wrapper recovers most of the loss without retraining the backbone.
core_hypothesis: On distorted projections these models produce errors that are a deterministic function of radial position (depth bowing tracking local focal-length variation), implying the failure is a projection mismatch rather than a representation gap, and is correctable by projection-aware resampling.

one_line_idea: Restricting test-time adaptation of video depth to per-sequence scale-shift-bias parameters under multi-view photometric consistency gives robust cross-domain gains where full-model TTA collapses.
core_hypothesis: Instability comes from adapting high-capacity weights on a biased self-supervised signal; constraining adaptation to a handful of affine parameters per sequence keeps the photometric signal identifiable and converts TTA from risky to reliably positive.

one_line_idea: Low-light depth degradation of foundation models is dominated by a structured, exposure-predictable bias rather than variance, so a tiny exposure-conditioned correction head recovers most of the loss without retraining.
core_hypothesis: Under low light, depth errors are mostly systematic (global underestimation of range and compression of far-field structure) and predictable from exposure statistics, so a small correction module conditioned on exposure features can restore a large fraction of accuracy.

one_line_idea: Small-baseline temporal parallax in casual video contains enough signal to resolve metric scale without IMU or intrinsics, and current video depth models fail to exploit it, as revealed by a parallax-ablation test.
core_hypothesis: Handheld jitter provides usable metric parallax; models trained with explicit multi-frame geometric losses can recover absolute scale from it, while current systems show near-zero sensitivity to parallax ablation, proving they ignore the signal.

one_line_idea: Ad hoc sky handling in depth training pipelines systematically distorts far-field geometry and horizon placement, and the distortion is measurable and correctable with a principled at-infinity parameterization.
core_hypothesis: Heuristic sky treatment biases the regression targets adjacent to the horizon, causing systematic overestimation compression of far-field depth and horizon-height errors, with the bias signature differing predictably by sky-handling scheme.

one_line_idea: Depth foundation models are substantially worse in the near-field manipulation zone (under 1 meter) than benchmark averages imply, because standard benchmarks under-sample exactly that range.
core_hypothesis: Training and evaluation range distributions under-represent near-field geometry, so relative error in the manipulation zone is a multiple of the benchmark average, with characteristic failures on foreshortening and defocus that range-stratified evaluation will expose.

one_line_idea: Optical flow benchmarks hide an unsolved motion-blur regime: blur-stratified evaluation will show error concentrating on high-blur pixels, where current models degrade to near-uselessness while averages look solved.
core_hypothesis: Fast motion produces blur that destroys the local evidence current matching-based architectures rely on; blur-stratified end-point error will reveal a severe unsolved regime invisible in aggregate statistics.

one_line_idea: Iterative recurrent refinement in flow architectures is largely an inference-time crutch: a single-pass global-matching model with a strong upsampler can match refinement-based accuracy at a fraction of latency on high-resolution video.
core_hypothesis: Refinement iterations mainly correct upsampling and initialization artifacts rather than performing essential inference, so investing the same compute in one-shot global matching plus a learned high-fidelity upsampling head reaches equal accuracy at much lower latency.

one_line_idea: Flow models track texture translation, not motion: on isoluminant color motion and other texture-decoupled stimuli they will fail catastrophically, exposing that learned flow lacks the motion-energy computation biological vision has.
core_hypothesis: Current models compute displacement of luminance texture; when motion is carried by chromatic contrast, contrast-envelope drift, or other second-order signals that humans perceive, learned models will report near-zero or wrong flow.

one_line_idea: On mostly-static scenes, point-tracking benchmark performance is largely explained by camera-geometry propagation, so learned trackers should be credited only for their margin over a depth-plus-pose geometric baseline.
core_hypothesis: For static-scene content, propagating points through estimated depth and camera pose reproduces most of the benchmark score; the learned tracker's real contribution concentrates on dynamic objects and occlusions, a much smaller pixel fraction than the metrics imply.

one_line_idea: Long-horizon point-tracking failures are dominated by re-identification errors after occlusion, not accumulated drift, so drift-focused architectural work targets the wrong failure mode.
core_hypothesis: Between occlusions, modern trackers drift negligibly; the bulk of long-horizon error arises at reappearance events where the tracker locks onto the wrong location, an error that is categorical rather than accumulative.

one_line_idea: Epipolar-constrained self-supervision on unlabeled real video can close most of the synthetic-to-real gap in optical flow, ending the field's structural dependence on synthetic training data.
core_hypothesis: For the static-scene majority of pixels, two-view geometry supplies an exact one-dimensional constraint (flow must lie on the epipolar line given estimated pose); training with this constraint plus photometric consistency and dynamic-region exclusion by residual analysis provides supervision strong enough to fine-tune synthetic-pretrained models into the real domain.

one_line_idea: Scalar end-point error hides direction errors that dominate downstream time-to-contact and steering computations, and a direction-magnitude decomposed evaluation reorders the flow leaderboard for safety-relevant use.
core_hypothesis: Models with similar end-point error differ widely in angular error distribution in the regions that matter for egomotion tasks, so leaderboard order does not predict downstream utility; a mechanism-level cause is that training losses penalize magnitude-weighted error, under-weighting slow-moving but direction-critical pixels.

one_line_idea: Explicit multi-hypothesis track states with a lightweight reappearance detector can match heavyweight learned-memory trackers on occlusion recovery at a fraction of compute, showing occlusion handling is a state-representation problem, not a capacity problem.
core_hypothesis: The essential requirement is representational: maintaining a small set of weighted location hypotheses through occlusion plus a discriminative reappearance test; given that state structure, a small model matches large-memory trackers on recovery accuracy because the hard part is not remembering appearance but representing multimodal position uncertainty.

one_line_idea: Monocular feed-forward 4D reconstruction now implies scene flow good enough to rival LiDAR-supervised methods for medium-range dynamics, collapsing a sensor requirement into a software capability.
core_hypothesis: Chaining dynamic-aware monocular reconstruction with temporal point correspondence yields metric 3D motion fields whose medium-range accuracy approaches LiDAR-supervised scene flow, because the binding constraint was geometry quality, which foundation reconstructors have largely fixed.

one_line_idea: Flow models carry a resolution-specific motion prior: evaluated off their training resolution they systematically underestimate large motions in a way predictable from correlation-volume truncation, not random degradation.
core_hypothesis: Displacement priors are baked in pixel units: at higher inference resolution the same physical motion becomes more pixels, exceeding the effective search range set by correlation-volume truncation and learned displacement statistics, producing systematic magnitude underestimation with a predictable onset.

one_line_idea: Point trackers trained on rigid-dominated data fail on non-rigid shear and stretching in a structured way: they snap to texture landmarks and refuse continuous deformation, measurable on procedurally deformed surfaces.
core_hypothesis: Under large non-rigid shear, trackers exhibit landmark capture: predictions cluster on distinctive texture points and systematically lag the true continuously deforming correspondence, an error signature distinct from random failure and diagnostic of a rigid-motion prior.

one_line_idea: Temporal context beyond two frames pays for itself almost entirely inside occluded regions: multi-frame flow gains are an occlusion-inpainting effect, and reporting occluded/visible strata separately will prove it and redirect multi-frame architecture design.
core_hypothesis: For visible pixels, two frames are nearly sufficient and extra context adds noise-averaging at best; for occluded pixels, extra frames enable motion extrapolation and reappearance evidence, so nearly all multi-frame improvement concentrates in the occluded stratum.

one_line_idea: Densify-and-split in Gaussian splatting is an implicit coarse-to-fine annealing schedule, and its scheduling, not the adaptive heuristics, carries most of the quality, testable by matched-budget schedule ablations.
core_hypothesis: The quality benefit comes from growing capacity gradually (an optimization annealing effect that avoids early overfitting to sparse view constraints), so a blind capacity schedule that adds primitives at random surface-plausible locations on the same timetable will match adaptive heuristics at equal final primitive count.

one_line_idea: Spherical-harmonic color in Gaussian splatting mostly compensates residual geometric error rather than modeling reflectance: fixing geometry with ground truth collapses the benefit of higher SH orders.
core_hypothesis: With imperfect primitive geometry, view-dependent color terms act as error absorbers that repaint view-specific misprojections; their contribution tracks geometric error, not material properties, so improving geometry should shrink the SH benefit sharply.

one_line_idea: Beyond a scene-dependent primitive budget, additional Gaussians fit view-sampling noise: interpolated-view metrics keep improving while extrapolated-view quality degrades, an overfitting signature current protocols never measure.
core_hypothesis: Excess primitives encode trajectory-specific photometric noise (exposure flicker, motion blur, misregistration), which improves interpolation metrics but actively harms rendering from genuinely novel viewpoints, making primitive count a classic capacity-overfitting axis.

one_line_idea: With opacity-entropy and surface-concentration regularization, splat scenes can serve as measurement-grade geometry, closing most of the surface-accuracy gap to multi-view-stereo pipelines while keeping real-time rendering.
core_hypothesis: The surface-accuracy gap comes from opacity spread and free-floating primitives, both controllable with regularizers that concentrate opacity mass near a 2D manifold; regularized training recovers most of the gap to dedicated MVS on standard geometry benchmarks without sacrificing rendering quality beyond a small margin.

one_line_idea: Anti-aliasing filters in splatting can be replaced by letting each primitive learn its own scale-space response, removing hand-derived filter approximations and their failure cases at extreme zoom.
core_hypothesis: A small learned per-primitive parameterization of appearance versus rendered footprint (a learned scale-space curve per Gaussian) can be optimized jointly with the scene and will match or beat analytic filters across zoom ranges, because the correct filter depends on scene content the analytic derivation ignores.

one_line_idea: Splatting failures on mirror-like surfaces are optimization pathologies, not representational limits: with reflection-consistent initialization the standard representation converges to virtual-image geometry that renders correctly from held-out views.
core_hypothesis: The photometric objective admits a good solution in which reflective surfaces are represented via virtual-image primitives behind the mirror plane; standard training misses it due to bad initialization and densification dynamics, not because the solution space lacks it.

one_line_idea: Stratified-random initialization plus aggressive pruning matches heuristic adaptive densification end-to-end, showing the celebrated densify-split-prune machinery is replaceable by capacity-then-selection.
core_hypothesis: An overcomplete start (random primitives stratified by a cheap depth or point prior) followed by opacity-based pruning explores at least as good a solution set as incremental densification, because selection from excess capacity is an easier optimization problem than incremental growth.

one_line_idea: Feed-forward splat predictors fail on camera-baseline distribution shift, not scene-content shift: their generalization boundary is a property of the training rig geometry, measurable by a baseline-sweep protocol.
core_hypothesis: These models internalize the training distribution of relative camera baselines and triangulation angles; quality degrades smoothly with content novelty but falls off a cliff outside the trained baseline range, because their matching and fusion layers are tuned to specific disparity statistics.

one_line_idea: Floater artifacts in splat reconstructions are primarily fossilized exposure and white-balance inconsistency, not sparse-view ambiguity: photometric-nuisance-controlled captures will eliminate most floaters at unchanged view counts.
core_hypothesis: Frame-to-frame photometric inconsistency creates view-specific residuals that the optimizer explains by placing low-opacity primitives in free space near the camera path; exposure variation, not view sparsity, is the dominant floater generator in typical captures.

one_line_idea: Dynamic splat representations interpolate time but cannot extrapolate it even fractions of a second, revealing they store appearance trajectories rather than motion models, measurable by a future-rendering cliff test.
core_hypothesis: These representations fit time-indexed appearance curves with no inductive bias toward physical motion continuation, so rendering quality collapses immediately outside the training time range, in contrast to even trivial constant-velocity geometric extrapolation.

one_line_idea: Popping artifacts in splat rendering are localized depth-ordering errors fixable by exact small-k per-tile sorting only where a cheap ambiguity test triggers, giving artifact-free video at a bounded few-percent cost.
core_hypothesis: Ordering errors that produce visible popping are spatially sparse and predictable from local depth-overlap statistics, so exact ordering applied selectively to flagged tiles eliminates perceptible popping at a small constant overhead, rather than requiring globally correct ordering.

one_line_idea: Implicit neural fields still beat explicit splats decisively on thin structures and view extrapolation, and a structure-stratified benchmark will show the representations are complements, not a settled succession.
core_hypothesis: Continuous implicit representations retain advantages precisely where primitive-based discretization is mismatched: sub-primitive thin geometry, smooth extrapolation beyond capture views, and topology-free surfaces; aggregate benchmarks under-weight these regimes.

one_line_idea: Feed-forward pointmap reconstructors carry strong absolute scene-scale priors and will misreconstruct scale-anomalous scenes (miniatures, sets, macro shots) in a predictable direction, revealing memorized scale rather than inferred geometry.
core_hypothesis: These models resolve scale primarily from semantic content statistics (rooms are room-sized), so on scale-anomalous scenes they will confidently output prior-consistent scale rather than geometry-consistent scale, and the error will follow the semantic prior direction.

one_line_idea: Multi-task 3D foundation models suffer measurable gradient conflict between depth and pose heads specifically on dynamic-scene batches, and conflict-gated task weighting recovers accuracy on both without new data.
core_hypothesis: On dynamic content the tasks disagree: pose heads need dynamic regions ignored while depth heads need them explained, producing systematic gradient conflict that damages both heads relative to conflict-managed training, with conflict magnitude spiking on dynamic batches.

one_line_idea: Neural surface reconstruction can reach near-GT-supervised accuracy using only photometric and multi-view consistency, and a controlled supervision-ablation study will locate exactly which scenes still need 3D ground truth.
core_hypothesis: For most scene types, the information in dense multi-view photometric consistency saturates what 3D supervision provides; the genuinely GT-dependent residual is confined to identifiable regimes (low texture, strong view-dependence), so self-supervised surface learning can match supervised accuracy outside those regimes.

one_line_idea: Scaling feed-forward 3D reconstruction is data-limited, not parameter-limited: multi-view scene data has low effective diversity per token, and a compute-matched scaling study will show exponents far below those driving 2D and language scaling optimism.
core_hypothesis: Reconstruction loss scales primarily with unique-scene count rather than total frames or parameters; frame-level scaling saturates quickly, making the effective scaling exponent with respect to compute much smaller than naive token counting suggests.

one_line_idea: Recurrent-memory reconstruction models have an effective spatial memory horizon of only a few keyframes: a loop-revisitation probe will show geometry consistency decaying with intervening content, exposing sequential state as the bottleneck for long-form 3D perception.
core_hypothesis: The recurrent state compresses recent observations well but overwrites older scene geometry roughly monotonically with new content volume, so revisited areas are re-reconstructed inconsistently unless revisitation is recent, with a measurable half-life in keyframes.

one_line_idea: Full cross-view attention in reconstruction transformers is mostly spent rediscovering epipolar geometry: constraining attention to epipolar neighborhoods after a coarse pose estimate retains accuracy at large compute savings.
core_hypothesis: After coarse pose estimation, the useful attention mass concentrates near epipolar-consistent token pairs; hard-restricting attention to dilated epipolar bands preserves nearly all reconstruction accuracy because off-band attention encodes redundant global context obtainable more cheaply.

one_line_idea: Single-image 3D generators are dominated by canonical-shape retrieval: counterfactual probes that decouple texture identity from geometric evidence will show outputs following the recognized category, not the visible geometry.
core_hypothesis: When visible geometric evidence (contours, shading, self-occlusion) contradicts the canonical shape of the recognized category, these models follow the category prior; genuine geometric evidence-following is limited to small deformations around templates.

one_line_idea: Rolling-shutter skew and motion blur are exploitable metric side channels: they encode absolute velocity and hence absolute scale, recoverable by a learned estimator to metrically calibrate monocular reconstruction without IMU or intrinsics.
core_hypothesis: Real cameras break the ambiguity: rolling-shutter row-time skew and exposure-time blur length are absolute-time-stamped measurements of image motion, and jointly with estimated relative geometry they determine metric scale; a learned extractor of these micro-cues can calibrate scale within useful bounds on ordinary video.

one_line_idea: Elaborate positional encodings in point cloud transformers are mostly redundant with kNN graph topology: an encoding-ablation study will show local connectivity carries the signal, collapsing a crowded design axis.
core_hypothesis: Once local neighborhoods are defined by kNN graph construction, most geometric information is already in the connectivity and edge vectors; sophisticated positional encodings mainly re-encode this, so radically simplified encodings will match performance across 3D tasks that do not require fine metric detail.

one_line_idea: Object-centric 3D pretraining transfers poorly to scene-level tasks because it learns closed-surface completion priors that actively mislead on open scene geometry, a measurable negative-transfer effect.
core_hypothesis: Object pretraining instills watertight-shape completion biases; scene data is open, partial, and clutter-dominated, so the prior misleads reconstruction and detection near occlusion boundaries, producing negative transfer that grows with pretraining strength on object data.

one_line_idea: Masked point-cloud pretraining learns sensor sampling patterns more than geometry: cross-sensor transfer tests will show performance collapse that tracks sampling-density mismatch rather than shape content.
core_hypothesis: The reconstruction pretext is solvable largely by modeling scan-pattern regularities (ring structure, density falloff, dropout patterns); representations therefore encode sensor signatures, and transfer across sensor types will degrade in proportion to sampling-statistics distance, even at identical scene geometry.

one_line_idea: Built-in rotation invariance in point cloud architectures destroys pose information that registration and manipulation actually need, and augmentation-trained equivariant-by-learning models dominate on a pose-sensitivity-stratified task suite.
core_hypothesis: Hard-wired invariance discards orientation information irreversibly; on pose-sensitive tasks (registration, grasp-relevant orientation estimation) invariant architectures underperform augmentation-trained standard architectures, and the deficit tracks how much task output depends on absolute or relative orientation.

one_line_idea: Lifting frozen 2D foundation features onto 3D points already saturates much of what 3D self-supervised learning achieves, so 3D SSL should be measured by its margin over the 2D-lifting baseline, which is rarely reported.
core_hypothesis: For RGB-paired 3D data, most representational value in current 3D SSL is semantic and already present in 2D features; the genuine 3D-specific margin (fine geometry, occlusion structure) is small and task-dependent, and honest baselines would reframe the subfield's progress narrative.

one_line_idea: Learned registration features fail in the low-overlap regime for a specific reason, local ambiguity without global layout reasoning, and overlap-stratified evaluation plus a layout-hypothesis stage will both prove and fix it.
core_hypothesis: Feature-based registration is fundamentally local: below an overlap threshold, correct correspondences exist but are statistically indistinguishable from ambiguous matches without scene-layout priors, so recall collapses sharply rather than degrading gracefully, and only global layout reasoning (room-shape priors, symmetry hypotheses) can push the frontier lower.

one_line_idea: Point cloud upsampling networks hallucinate plausible-looking surface detail that measurably corrupts downstream pose estimation and registration, making upsampling a negative-value preprocessing step for geometric pipelines.
core_hypothesis: Upsamplers interpolate with shape priors that are wrong in the tails; the hallucinated points carry confident but biased geometry that downstream estimators weight as evidence, degrading registration and pose accuracy relative to running directly on the sparse input.

one_line_idea: Discarding range-image structure by converting scans to unordered points throws away the sensor noise model, and architectures that retain scan-grid structure will beat point-set models on odometry at matched capacity.
core_hypothesis: Sensor noise is structured in the acquisition grid (range-dependent per-beam noise, incidence-angle effects); models operating on range images can learn implicit per-measurement reliability weighting that point-set models cannot recover after unordering, yielding better odometry and mapping accuracy especially in high-noise regimes.

one_line_idea: Content-adaptive keyframe selection, not longer context, is the binding constraint in long-video understanding: a learned selector at 10% frame budget can retain nearly all of full-context accuracy across video reasoning tasks.
core_hypothesis: Information relevant to video-level understanding is concentrated in a small, identifiable subset of frames; a query-conditioned selector trained to maximize downstream answer quality can find it, making frame budget a soft constraint and context-length competition mostly wasteful.

one_line_idea: For revisitation-heavy long videos, a geometric 3D scene buffer beats learned appearance-token memories of the SAM2 style at re-localizing content after long absences, because place is a stronger long-horizon key than appearance.
core_hypothesis: Registering observations into a persistent metric 3D buffer (via online reconstruction and camera tracking) provides a memory keyed by place rather than appearance recency; for content re-identification after long absences in the same environment, place-keyed lookup will beat appearance-token memory at matched compute, with the advantage growing with absence duration.

one_line_idea: Long-video benchmarks are answerable from tiny frame subsets: an oracle frame-selection audit will show most questions need under 1% of frames, meaning the benchmarks measure retrieval, not long-form temporal understanding.
core_hypothesis: For most benchmark questions, there exists a tiny frame subset sufficient for a frozen model to answer correctly; question types genuinely requiring cross-video integration (duration reasoning, repeated-event counting, narrative causality across acts) are a small minority, so long-context gains reported on these benchmarks mostly reflect better retrieval.

one_line_idea: Video foundation models are near chance at judging the arrow of time on physics-driven footage, a capability gap invisible to every mainstream benchmark and decisive for world-model claims.
core_hypothesis: Because pretraining objectives are nearly symmetric under time reversal and human-edited video contains reversed and looped content, current video representations encode little arrow-of-time signal; probes will be near chance on physics-driven clips while succeeding on clips with semantic directionality cues (people walking forward).

one_line_idea: Event-order understanding in video-language models rides on editing artifacts: on continuous single-shot footage their before/after accuracy will collapse, revealing shot grammar, not temporal reasoning, as the learned mechanism.
core_hypothesis: Models learned to read editing grammar (shot changes, framing conventions, montage patterns) as an order signal; on unedited continuous footage where order must be inferred from state changes in the world, before/after accuracy will drop toward chance while edited-footage accuracy stays high.

one_line_idea: Storing motion state (tracked positions, velocities, and a sparse dynamics summary) instead of appearance tokens halves video-memory cost at equal long-horizon tracking accuracy, because appearance is re-observable but motion history is not.
core_hypothesis: Appearance information is largely recoverable from the current frame plus a compact identity code, while motion history (velocities, trajectories through occlusion) is unrecoverable once discarded; a memory that prioritizes kinematic state over appearance snapshots achieves equal or better long-horizon tracking and re-identification at a fraction of the storage.

one_line_idea: Video models encode absolute frame rate as a hidden covariate: speed-perception probes will reveal systematic bias when test frame rate differs from the training distribution, corrupting all downstream motion judgments.
core_hypothesis: Models internalize the modal training frame rate as an implicit clock; motion-speed judgments, action-duration estimates, and dynamics predictions all inherit a multiplicative bias equal to the train-test frame-rate ratio, rather than being frame-rate invariant.

one_line_idea: Repetitive-action counting is already latent in frozen video features as periodic token-trajectory structure, extractable by spectral analysis without any counting-specific training.
core_hypothesis: Repetitive motion imprints periodic structure on the trajectory of frame and patch tokens through feature space; frequency-domain analysis of these trajectories recovers repetition frequency and count without supervision, and count accuracy from frozen features will approach trained counting systems.

one_line_idea: The egocentric-video performance gap is mostly a camera-motion-statistics gap, not a content gap: motion-matched resampling of exocentric data will close much of it without collecting new egocentric footage.
core_hypothesis: The transfer gap is dominated by unfamiliar camera-motion statistics (head-driven rotation, motion parallax patterns) rather than by unfamiliar content; augmenting or resampling exocentric data to match egocentric motion statistics recovers a large share of the gap at zero collection cost.

one_line_idea: Pixel-space next-frame prediction spends its capacity on texture advection, not dynamics: a loss-decomposition study will show physics-relevant errors are a vanishing share of the training signal, explaining why video predictors fail physics probes despite low loss.
core_hypothesis: The pixel loss is dominated by texture transport terms (most pixels move predictably with local flow), while dynamics-decisive pixels (contact events, direction changes, occlusion births) contribute negligibly to the gradient; consequently optimization converges to advection engines with no pressure to model dynamics, and the loss-share imbalance quantitatively predicts the physics-probe failure.

one_line_idea: Object permanence in video trackers and memory models fails past a measurable occlusion-duration threshold, and the failure is architectural (memory decay) rather than perceptual, testable by a duration-sweep protocol with location prediction through occlusion.
core_hypothesis: Permanence-like behavior in current systems is short-horizon memory persistence, not object-state inference: predicted-location accuracy through occlusion decays smoothly with duration and collapses beyond a threshold set by memory capacity and decay dynamics, while systems with explicit dynamics state (even simple constant-velocity models) degrade far more slowly.

one_line_idea: Feed-forward dynamic-scene reconstruction can match per-scene-optimized 4D methods on geometry metrics within a bounded gap while being orders faster, making optimization-based 4D a transitional technology, and the gap map tells us where optimization still pays.
core_hypothesis: For the geometry that downstream consumers use (depth, 3D trajectories, camera poses), feed-forward dynamic reconstructors already sit within a modest, quantifiable gap of optimization methods on most scene types, with the true optimization advantage confined to identifiable regimes (long sequences, extreme deformation, fine view-dependent detail).

one_line_idea: Piecewise-rigid motion priors generalize to fast, unfamiliar dynamics better than learned free-form deformation fields, and a motion-magnitude-stratified 3D tracking comparison will show the crossover point where learned flexibility becomes a liability.
core_hypothesis: Physical scenes are dominated by piecewise-rigid motion; free-form deformation fields buy accuracy on soft deformation at the cost of catastrophic failure on fast rigid motion outside training statistics, while piecewise-rigid parameterizations degrade gracefully everywhere, creating a measurable regime crossover.

one_line_idea: Discrete keyframe-based 4D representations with learned interpolators beat continuously time-conditioned fields on rapidly changing scenes, because continuous conditioning imposes an implicit temporal smoothness prior that fast dynamics violate.
core_hypothesis: Networks conditioned on continuous time coordinates spectrally bias toward slow temporal variation, systematically underfitting rapid transitions (impacts, direction reversals); keyframed discrete states with learned interpolation allocate capacity at transitions and will win on motion-transient-heavy content at matched budgets.

one_line_idea: Camera-object motion separation in monocular dynamic reconstruction degenerates predictably under near-forward camera motion, and quantifying the degeneracy prevalence in real corpora will show it affects a large share of driving and walking footage.
core_hypothesis: For forward-translating cameras (driving, walking), objects moving along the camera axis produce image motion nearly indistinguishable from static geometry at wrong depth; methods silently resolve the ambiguity with priors, producing confident depth-speed errors whose prevalence in real footage is high and unmeasured.

one_line_idea: Transporting a fixed set of Gaussians along estimated scene flow, instead of re-densifying per timestep, reconstructs dynamic scenes with severalfold fewer primitives at equal quality, because dynamic scenes reuse geometry that current 4D methods keep re-creating.
core_hypothesis: Physical persistence means the primitive set should be nearly constant with only poses changing; coupling a persistent primitive set to an explicit 3D motion field (transport instead of respawn) matches rendering and geometry quality at a fraction of primitive count and naturally yields 3D trajectories as a byproduct.

one_line_idea: Temporal smoothing losses that make video depth look stable actively destroy true depth change, and an approach-sequence evaluation (time-to-contact fidelity) will show stabilized models are worse than their unstabilized versions for dynamic consumers.
core_hypothesis: Consistency losses penalize genuine depth changes (approaching objects, camera push-in) as if they were noise, biasing models toward temporal inertia; on sequences with real depth dynamics, stabilized models will systematically lag true depth change, corrupting derived quantities like time-to-contact that safety consumers rely on.

one_line_idea: Classical low-rank trajectory bases still beat learned motion representations for non-rigid structure recovery on low-texture deformable objects, defining a data-regime boundary the deep 4D literature ignores.
core_hypothesis: Low-rank temporal structure is a strong, correct prior for many deformables (cloth, faces, organs); when texture is too poor for learned correspondence to shine, classical basis constraints extract more from the same observations, and a texture-by-method comparison will show a crossover the field assumes away.

one_line_idea: Dynamic novel-view benchmarks are dominated by photometric quality variance rather than geometric fidelity: re-scoring published-style comparisons with geometry-only metrics will reorder methods and change which research directions look promising.
core_hypothesis: Method ranking variance on dynamic benchmarks is mostly attributable to appearance-modeling differences (color calibration, detail hallucination), so geometry-only re-evaluation (depth, trajectory, and camera accuracy) will produce substantially different orderings, revealing that the community optimizes appearance while believing it optimizes 4D structure.

one_line_idea: Defocus gradients across the frame are a single-image focal-length oracle: a probe exploiting depth-of-field structure will estimate intrinsics better than semantic-cue baselines, upgrading uncalibrated 3D pipelines for free.
core_hypothesis: The spatial pattern of defocus blur across an image is jointly determined by aperture, focal length, and scene depth; combined with a monocular depth estimate, measurable defocus gradients over-constrain focal length, giving a physics-based estimator that works in structure-free natural scenes where geometric cues vanish.

one_line_idea: Visual gravity-direction estimation from object and scene priors can reach IMU-competitive accuracy on typical footage, enabling orientation-aware vision on the billions of cameras without inertial data streams.
core_hypothesis: Scenes are saturated with gravity witnesses (standing people, hanging objects, liquid surfaces, architectural verticals, tree growth); a learned estimator aggregating these cues can recover gravity direction within about one degree for the large majority of frames on ordinary footage, sufficient for most downstream uses of IMU gravity.

one_line_idea: Out-of-distribution failure in learned camera pose regression is substantially a rotation-parameterization artifact: controlled parameterization swaps will show geodesic-aware outputs generalizing far better than the field's default choices at identical backbones.
core_hypothesis: Parameterizations differ in how regression errors map onto the rotation manifold; under distribution shift, extrapolation in the output space dominates failure, so manifold-respecting parameterizations degrade gracefully while chart-based ones fail at chart boundaries, producing large OOD differences invisible in-distribution.

one_line_idea: Learned feature matchers win correspondence recall but lose sub-pixel precision to classical refinement: a hybrid that re-refines learned matches with classical photometric optimization will cut bundle-adjustment residuals without losing robustness.
core_hypothesis: Robustness (finding the right coarse match) and precision (localizing it to hundredths of a pixel) are separable problems: learned matchers solve the first, classical least-squares patch alignment solves the second, and chaining them will reduce reprojection residuals and camera-pose error over either alone, especially in wide-baseline and day-night conditions.

one_line_idea: Non-overlapping multi-camera rigs can be extrinsically calibrated to sub-degree accuracy using only a shared ground plane and per-camera odometry, removing the overlap requirement that constrains rig design.
core_hypothesis: Each camera independently observes two shared references: the ground plane (constraining roll, pitch, height) and the rig's rigid motion (per-camera visual odometry must be related by the fixed extrinsics); jointly these over-constrain full six-degree extrinsics without any shared field of view, to accuracy sufficient for downstream fusion.

one_line_idea: The self-supervised depth-flow-pose triad is not saturated: joint reliability weighting across the three estimators (each downweighting pixels where the others disagree) yields large gains in adverse conditions where each alone degrades unpredictably.
core_hypothesis: The triad's mutual geometric consistency provides a per-pixel reliability signal richer than any single-model confidence: pixels where depth-flow-pose closure fails identify which estimator is failing and where, enabling adaptive reweighting that improves all three estimates in hard conditions without any new labels.

one_line_idea: Novel-view-synthesis metric families disagree enough to flip method rankings at publication-relevant margins, and a metric-agreement audit across the published method spectrum will quantify how much NVS progress is metric-choice artifact.
core_hypothesis: The three standard metric families weight blur, hallucinated detail, and color fidelity differently enough that method rankings are unstable within typical claimed margins; a fraction of published pairwise superiority claims would reverse under a different standard metric, making metric choice a hidden researcher degree of freedom.

one_line_idea: Chamfer distance is blind to topological errors that decide downstream success: a topology-aware reconstruction metric validated against robot navigation and interaction outcomes will re-rank reconstruction methods by fitness for use.
core_hypothesis: A metric family combining distance with topological agreement (connectivity, holes, passage structure relative to GT) will predict downstream task success (simulated navigation, grasp planning) far better than chamfer and F-score, and will materially re-rank published reconstruction methods.

one_line_idea: Point-tracking benchmark averages hide that leading models are still poor on thin structures and self-similar textures: difficulty-stratified re-annotation of existing benchmarks will reveal large headroom the leaderboard says does not exist.
core_hypothesis: Aggregate scores are dominated by easy points (large textured surfaces); annotating existing benchmarks with per-point difficulty attributes will reveal strata (thin structures, repeated patterns, fast rotation) where accuracy remains far below the average, with consistent cross-model failure patterns indicating shared architectural blind spots.

one_line_idea: The claimed closure of the synthetic-to-real gap in optical flow does not survive rolling-shutter and exposure realities: real-camera-artifact-stratified evaluation will reopen the gap that clean benchmark transfers declared closed.
core_hypothesis: Consumer video differs from both synthetic data and clean benchmarks through acquisition artifacts (rolling shutter skew, auto-exposure fluctuation, compression); flow accuracy on artifact-rich real footage degrades substantially, so the gap was redefined, not closed, and artifact simulation in training will recover much of the loss.

one_line_idea: Label-free evaluation of video and 3D perception via internal geometric consistency (reconstruction closure across views and time) correlates strongly with supervised rankings, enabling benchmark-free model selection on any target domain.
core_hypothesis: For geometric tasks, correctness has an internal signature: outputs of a good model are mutually consistent under reprojection, temporal transport, and loop closure on unlabeled target footage; a consistency score computed from these closures will rank models nearly as well as ground-truth benchmarks do, because large violations of internal consistency cannot coexist with accuracy.

one_line_idea: LLM tool routing in vision-agent frameworks follows tool-description semantics rather than measured tool competence: swapping two overlapping tools' natural-language descriptions redirects most calls while implementations stay fixed.
core_hypothesis: The controller's routing decision is a function of description text that is largely invariant to the tools' true competence, because the loop has no channel through which execution outcomes can correct description-driven priors within or across sessions.

one_line_idea: Vision-agent controllers cannot consume numeric tool metadata: decisive detector scores or OCR quality values injected into tool outputs change downstream decisions in only a small fraction of cases where they should flip the decision.
core_hypothesis: Controllers treat numeric metadata as filler text: on instances constructed so the metadata is decisive under the task rubric, decisions track the numbers far below what a rational reader would achieve, and coarse verbal quantizers (high/medium/low) outperform the raw numbers they summarize.

one_line_idea: When-to-call-a-tool decisions improve more from a two-line self-probe ('answer without the tool, then estimate what the tool would add') than from scaling the controller model.
core_hypothesis: Marginal-benefit estimation is latent in the controller and elicitable: forcing a draft answer plus an explicit expected-gain statement before any tool call aligns tool usage with actual marginal utility, recovering a large share of oracle-routing performance without any model change.

one_line_idea: Vision-agent answers depend on tool call order even when evidence is commutative: permuting the order of independent tool calls flips final answers at a rate comparable to swapping the controller model itself.
core_hypothesis: Because each tool result conditions interpretation of later results in the transcript, final answers are systematically order-sensitive, and the magnitude of this order effect rivals differences attributed to controller choice.

one_line_idea: Routing policies can improve without human labels by fine-tuning the controller on its own execution traces filtered by end-task self-consistency, because traces contain enough outcome signal to supervise tool choice.
core_hypothesis: Traces where independent runs agree on the final answer are enriched for correct routing decisions, so consistency-filtered traces form a usable self-supervised dataset: a small controller LoRA-tuned on them improves routing on held-out tasks with zero human labels.

one_line_idea: System accuracy versus toolbox size is non-monotone: pruning a vision-agent's toolbox with a held-out marginal-utility score beats the full toolbox, because overlapping tools create routing confusion that outweighs coverage gains.
core_hypothesis: There is an interior optimum in toolbox size: beyond it, marginal coverage is smaller than marginal confusion, and a simple per-tool marginal-utility estimate (accuracy with vs without the tool on a pilot set) identifies a pruned toolbox that dominates the full one.

one_line_idea: LLM controllers are near-chance at detecting silently corrupted tool outputs, but a cheap paired-call wrapper (re-run the tool on a jittered input and compare) restores most detection without touching the controller.
core_hypothesis: Silent tool-failure detection is nearly impossible from a single textual report but easy from report stability: corrupted or failing tool executions are far less stable under small input jitter than healthy ones, so a compare-two-calls wrapper exposes failures the controller cannot see.

one_line_idea: Auto-generated 'competence cards' — per-tool accuracy profiles measured on a small probe suite and inserted into the controller prompt — improve routing more than hand-written tool descriptions.
core_hypothesis: A standardized probe suite run once per tool yields a compact empirical competence card (strong on X, fails on Y-type inputs), and conditioning the controller on cards instead of descriptions moves routing toward competence-anchored decisions measurably.

one_line_idea: Orchestration prompts and routing policies tuned on one controller LLM transfer poorly to another: the cross-controller transfer penalty exceeds the tuning gain itself, making agent-framework results controller-specific claims.
core_hypothesis: Scaffold tuning is controller-specific adaptation: most of the gain from tuning a vision-agent scaffold on controller A disappears or reverses when the scaffold is run with controller B, so scaffold and controller form a coupled system that must be evaluated jointly.

one_line_idea: The text interface between vision tools and the controller imposes a measurable information ceiling: a probe trained to answer spatial questions from the loop's textual intermediates plateaus far below one trained on the tool's raw outputs.
core_hypothesis: For spatially structured tasks, the verbalization step is the binding constraint: the achievable accuracy from textual intermediates is capped well below the accuracy achievable from the raw tool outputs they summarize, independent of controller strength.

one_line_idea: Prose tool reports cause downstream attribute hallucination: a traceable share of final-answer errors originates at the verbalization step rather than in the vision tool or the controller's reasoning, and structured key-value reports cut this error class.
core_hypothesis: Verbalization is an active error source, not a neutral channel: fluent prose reports inject unsupported attributes at a measurable rate, these injections propagate to final answers, and replacing prose with minimal key-value reports removes the injected-attribute error class without losing task-relevant content.

one_line_idea: Information loss across chained text handoffs compounds superlinearly: two verbalization steps lose more than twice one step's information, because each step re-summarizes an already-lossy summary.
core_hypothesis: Each verbalization step drops details that later steps would have needed to summarize faithfully, so the second hop degrades disproportionately: relay loss grows superlinearly with hop count, and the compounding factor is stable enough to characterize as an interface law.

one_line_idea: Replacing the text handoff between a vision tool and the controller with a small learned adapter that injects continuous tokens recovers most of the interface-lost accuracy, isolating discretization — not controller reasoning — as the binding constraint.
core_hypothesis: A lightweight adapter mapping tool feature vectors to a few soft tokens in the controller's embedding space preserves the spatial detail text drops; the recovery it achieves directly measures how much of the loop's failure was interface discretization rather than reasoning capacity. This is an architecture change justified by a specific mechanism claim: the loss is located at the discretization step.

one_line_idea: Making tool reports question-aware — forwarding the user question to the tool's report generator — beats upgrading to a larger controller, because relevance filtering at the interface dominates reasoning capacity downstream.
core_hypothesis: The single highest-leverage bit of context at the interface is the question itself: question-conditioned reports allocate the text channel to task-relevant content, and this interface fix yields larger end-task gains than swapping in a controller one size class larger.

one_line_idea: Referring-expression drift is a loop failure, not a VLM failure: multi-turn agents lose object identity as similar-object count grows, and assigning persistent visual IDs (numbered marks) at first sight eliminates most identity errors without changing any model.
core_hypothesis: Identity maintenance through descriptive text is the failure mechanism: identity-error rate rises with the count of similar distractors and with turns elapsed since first mention, and a persistent numbered-mark scheme (stamp IDs at first detection, reuse everywhere) removes the text-decay pathway.

one_line_idea: Agent pipelines exhibit round-number bias in quantitative visual estimates that single-pass VLMs do not: repeated verbalization quantizes sizes, counts, and distances toward salient round values, and the bias grows with loop depth.
core_hypothesis: Verbalization steps act as attractors toward round and culturally salient numbers; the excess mass at round values grows with the number of restatements, making loop depth a causal variable for quantitative bias independent of the underlying VLM's perception.

one_line_idea: For multi-step visual tasks, storing history as image crops beats storing text summaries at matched context budget: text memory, not context length, is the binding constraint on long-horizon visual agents.
core_hypothesis: Deferring interpretation preserves option value: raw crop memory lets the agent re-extract whatever a later question needs, while text memory commits early to one interpretation; at equal token budgets, crop memory wins on tasks whose later steps depend on earlier visual detail.

one_line_idea: Self-consistency voting saturates almost immediately for perception-bound questions because samples share the same wrong percept: the accuracy-vs-samples curve flattens by k=4 while reasoning-bound questions keep climbing.
core_hypothesis: For questions whose difficulty lies in perception, error is locked in at encoding: resampled generations vary in wording but share the percept, so vote diversity is fake and gains saturate at tiny k, unlike reasoning-bound questions where paths genuinely diverge.

one_line_idea: Longer reasoning chains between looking and answering degrade fine-grained visual accuracy: forced chain length causally increases detail errors, indicating that verbal reasoning overwrites visual detail in the loop's working state.
core_hypothesis: Visual detail available at answer time decays with the number of intervening generated tokens: forcing longer chains (padding with topically relevant but non-informative reasoning) causally lowers accuracy on detail-critical questions, with a monotone dose-response.

one_line_idea: For perception-bound tasks, spending test-time compute on re-looking (fresh encodes of question-relevant crops) dominates spending it on re-thinking (more reasoning tokens) at every matched budget point.
core_hypothesis: Perception-bound accuracy is limited by what was encoded, so marginal compute converts to accuracy at a higher rate through re-encoding question-relevant crops than through generating more reasoning tokens; the re-look curve dominates the re-think curve across budgets.

one_line_idea: An allocation policy that spends crops and samples per-instance based on a cheap difficulty probe beats uniform allocation at fixed total budget, because the marginal utility of test-time compute varies by an order of magnitude across instances.
core_hypothesis: A two-signal difficulty probe (draft-answer stability across 2 cheap samples, plus target-size estimate) predicts per-instance marginal utility well enough that adaptive reallocation of a fixed budget strictly dominates uniform spending.

one_line_idea: Iterative zooming is an anytime algorithm with a predictable profile: the first zoom captures most of the achievable gain on natural-image tasks, and only small-object long-tail tasks keep gaining past two steps.
core_hypothesis: Zoom-gain profiles are strongly front-loaded and task-family-dependent in a systematic way: the fraction of total achievable gain captured at step one is high for typical scenes and falls predictably as the ratio of target size to image size shrinks.

one_line_idea: A task decomposability score predicts when deep agent loops with a small VLM beat a large VLM at matched FLOPs: loops win only above a decomposability threshold, and the crossover is stable across task families.
core_hypothesis: The deciding variable is decomposability — the degree to which a task factors into independently checkable visual subgoals; a score computed from a small pilot (accuracy gain from oracle sub-question decomposition) predicts the loop-vs-scale winner before building either system.

one_line_idea: Voting over agent-chosen image transformations beats voting over random augmentations at equal vote count: choosing which views to aggregate is itself a perceptual skill the loop can exploit.
core_hypothesis: An agent that inspects the image and names its suspected failure mode selects transformation sets whose votes are decorrelated where it matters, beating random augmentation voting at matched vote counts — the gain measuring a real introspective-perception capability of the loop.

one_line_idea: Most of a perception loop's gain can be distilled into a single forward pass by fine-tuning on the loop's own successful traces, implying the loop is primarily a data generator rather than an inference-time necessity.
core_hypothesis: Loop gains on perception tasks come mostly from a re-usable policy (where to look, what to check) rather than from irreducible per-instance search, so LoRA-tuning the base VLM on consistency-filtered loop traces transfers most of the gain into a single pass.

one_line_idea: Perception tasks split into compute-limited and representation-limited families with a measurable signature: cross-sample answer variance under test-time compute predicts whether any loop can help, before running any loop.
core_hypothesis: When the encoder's representation contains the answer but decoding is noisy, samples disagree (high variance) and loops help; when the representation lacks the answer, samples agree on the same error (low variance, wrong mode) and no loop built on the same encoder can help — variance under cheap sampling is therefore a regime detector.

one_line_idea: Self-correction in vision agents fixes reasoning slips but not perception errors: revision rates conditioned on error type are strongly asymmetric because the loop re-reads its own percept instead of re-perceiving.
core_hypothesis: Revision operates on the verbal trace, not on the image: errors introduced during reasoning are detectable and correctable from text alone, while errors introduced at perception are invisible to the loop, producing a large, stable revision-rate asymmetry by error type.

one_line_idea: Below a measurable critic-precision threshold, verify-then-revise loops are net negative: flips from correct to wrong outnumber repairs, and the break-even precision can be estimated in advance from the flip matrix.
core_hypothesis: Revision behavior is governed by a simple accounting identity over the flip matrix (repair rate times error mass vs corruption rate times correct mass); the break-even critic precision derived from a small pilot predicts whether any given critic will help or hurt at scale.

one_line_idea: Requiring critics to cite pixel evidence — a crop or mark accompanying every objection — turns marginal verification loops into positive ones, because ungrounded objections drive most wrong flips.
core_hypothesis: The damage in verification loops is concentrated in evidence-free objections; imposing an evidence-citation contract (every objection must attach the region it is about) suppresses confabulated critiques more than it suppresses true ones, moving the loop's flip matrix to net positive.

one_line_idea: Structured visual outputs should be verified visually: rendering predicted boxes or layouts back onto the image and asking a fresh model 'is this consistent' catches error classes that text-based verification of the same predictions never flags.
core_hypothesis: Re-rendering closes the loop through perception: a verifier that sees the prediction drawn on the image detects geometric and relational errors that are undetectable from coordinates-as-text, adding a complementary error channel rather than a redundant one.

one_line_idea: Self-verification loops have attractors: iterating verify-revise converges within a few steps to answers that are stable but wrong on a measurable fraction of instances, and convergence speed does not predict correctness.
core_hypothesis: Verify-revise dynamics form a map with multiple attractors determined by the model's priors and the transcript, not by the image; a non-trivial fraction of instances converge to stable wrong answers from any reasonable start, and convergence speed is uninformative about which attractor was reached.

one_line_idea: Verifying visual claims via entailed consequence questions ('if X, then Y should be visible — check Y') outperforms direct re-asking, because consequence checks decorrelate the verifier's percept from the proposer's.
core_hypothesis: Claims about images entail secondary observables (shadows, occlusion patterns, co-occurring parts, geometric consequences); querying those observables engages different visual evidence than the original question, so consequence-based verification detects false claims that direct re-asking confirms.

one_line_idea: Revision gains decay geometrically across rounds with a stable ratio: one revision captures most of the achievable repair, making multi-round self-correction schedules mostly wasted compute.
core_hypothesis: The population of repairable errors is exhausted front-first: errors fixable by the loop's mechanism get fixed in round one, and later rounds churn on unfixable (perception-borne) errors, producing a geometric decay in marginal gain with a ratio stable across tasks and models.

one_line_idea: A small library of specialized critics keyed to a fixed visual-error taxonomy (mislocalization, miscount, attribute swap, relation flip, hallucinated object) beats one general critic at equal cost, because critic instructions act as error priors.
core_hypothesis: Critique is a detection problem with a prior: routing each output to type-specialized critics (or running a cheap type classifier first) concentrates the verifier's capacity on the likely failure, raising detection at fixed compute relative to one broad critic.

one_line_idea: Verifiers inherit proposer percepts through the transcript: verifiers shown only the image and the bare answer catch more perception errors than verifiers shown the full chain-of-thought, reversing the assumed value of context.
core_hypothesis: Transcript exposure induces percept inheritance: a verifier that reads the proposer's description of the image tends to see the image that way, so blinding the verifier to everything except image and answer forces an independent look and raises perception-error detection.

one_line_idea: Step-level verification of intermediate tool outputs beats final-answer verification for multi-step visual tasks at matched verification budget, and the advantage grows with chain length.
core_hypothesis: Errors are cheapest to catch where they enter: intermediate tool outputs are small, concrete, and checkable against the image, so allocating the same verification compute across steps instead of the final answer yields higher end-task accuracy, with the advantage scaling in chain depth.

one_line_idea: Most visual-program failures collapse into a short list of primitive-misuse patterns, so a fixed library of about ten automatic repair rules recovers a large share of failed executions without improving the planner.
core_hypothesis: The failure distribution over program executions is heavy-headed: a compact rule library targeting the top misuse patterns (detected from execution traces, applied as automatic rewrites) recovers a substantial fraction of failures at negligible cost, bounding how much planner intelligence is actually missing.

one_line_idea: Program abstractions assume deterministic subroutines, but resampling stochastic primitives flips visual-program answers at a rate that rivals planner-quality differences, making single-run program evaluations unstable as system claims.
core_hypothesis: Answer identity under primitive resampling is fragile in proportion to program depth and to how many primitives sit on the answer's critical path; the induced answer-flip rate is large enough to rival gaps attributed to planner choice, so program behavior is a distribution, not a value.

one_line_idea: Visual programs are less faithful than they look: when a primitive fails silently, controllers often emit answers from language priors while presenting them as program outputs, and counterfactual step-perturbation quantifies how often execution is bypassed.
core_hypothesis: Execution bypass is common and measurable: counterfactually flipping a decisive intermediate output should flip the answer under faithful execution, so the rate of unchanged answers under decisive flips directly measures how often the program is theater.

one_line_idea: Real query streams concentrate on few program skeletons, so caching and re-instantiating the top skeletons amortizes synthesis: coverage-vs-cache-size follows a heavy-tailed law exploitable for systems.
core_hypothesis: Abstracting synthesized programs into slotted skeletons reveals a heavy-tailed reuse distribution; retrieving and re-instantiating cached skeletons for matching queries cuts synthesis errors and latency while covering most traffic with a small cache.

one_line_idea: Adding a lightweight type system over visual-program primitives (region, entity-set, scalar, boolean) prevents a major share of wrong answers, because type confusion at step boundaries — not planning — is the dominant failure.
core_hypothesis: A four-type discipline with checked coercions at step boundaries converts silent wrong answers into either correct coercions or loud failures that trigger resynthesis; the wrong-answer reduction it achieves measures how much of the paradigm's error mass is boundary confusion rather than bad plans.

one_line_idea: Planners told each primitive's empirical error profile write different and better programs — inserting redundancy and cross-checks where primitives are weak — showing program synthesis should condition on tool reliability, not just tool signatures.
core_hypothesis: Injecting measured per-primitive error profiles into the synthesis prompt changes plan structure in predictable directions (redundant paths around weak primitives, cheap existence checks before expensive chains, preference for reliable primitives at critical nodes) and those structural changes improve end-task accuracy.

one_line_idea: Visual programs are their own data engines: executing synthesized programs on procedurally generated scenes yields verified supervision that fine-tunes the planner, improving synthesis on real queries without human labels.
core_hypothesis: A closed self-improvement loop — synthesize programs, execute on procedural scenes with known state, keep programs whose outputs match scene ground truth, fine-tune the planner on the survivors — transfers to real-image queries because program structure, not scene texture, is what the planner learns.

one_line_idea: Visual programs make failures locally attributable in a way chain-of-thought does not: automatic step-level attribution on synthetic scenes assigns blame to the true faulty step far above chance, enabling targeted fixes impossible for monolithic VLMs.
core_hypothesis: Because each program step has a checkable input-output contract, automatic attribution (replay each step against synthetic-scene ground truth) localizes the true fault at rates far above the 1/steps chance baseline — and this localization accuracy is the measurable content of the paradigm's interpretability claim.

one_line_idea: Annotation agents make correlated errors across seeds and prompt variants, so self-agreement massively overestimates label quality: unanimous agent labels stay wrong at rates that would be impossible for independent human annotators.
core_hypothesis: Agent errors are systematically shared (same training data, same percepts), so the unanimity-implies-quality inference fails quantitatively: agreement among agent runs is nearly uninformative about correctness on the error-prone slice, unlike agreement among humans.

one_line_idea: Cheap-proposer/expensive-verifier annotation cascades trace a predictable cost-quality frontier: verifying only flagged or disagreeing items achieves near full-expensive quality at a fraction of cost, and the frontier shape is estimable from a small pilot.
core_hypothesis: Disagreement and instability signals from the cheap tier identify most of its errors, so a cascade routing only that slice to the expensive tier sits near the expensive model's quality at a small fraction of its cost — and a 200-item pilot suffices to predict the full frontier before committing budget.

one_line_idea: Iterative self-labeling loops (train on agent labels, relabel with the trained model, retrain) amplify the agent's initial systematic biases at a measurable per-round rate rather than washing them out, producing datasets that look cleaner and are more biased each round.
core_hypothesis: Random label noise shrinks across rounds while systematic bias compounds: any consistent initial tendency (boundary conventions, class confusions, attribute defaults) gets reinforced each cycle, so apparent quality (agreement, confidence) rises while distance from human ground truth on the biased dimensions grows.

one_line_idea: Annotation agents allowed to request extra evidence (zoomed crops, alternate frames) on self-flagged hard instances beat fixed-pipeline agents at matched cost, because evidence acquisition — not model quality — limits label accuracy on the hard tail.
core_hypothesis: The hard tail of annotation error is evidence-limited: giving the agent an evidence-request action (zoom, adjacent frame, enhanced view) with a budget reallocated from the easy majority cuts tail error more than upgrading the annotation model at the same total cost.

one_line_idea: Label provenance is recoverable: a classifier can distinguish models trained on agent-labeled versus human-labeled data using only behavioral probes, enabling post-hoc audits of dataset supply chains.
core_hypothesis: Agent labels carry systematic signatures (boundary conventions, confusion structure, tail treatment, round-number artifacts) that persist through training into model behavior, so a probe suite over a trained model separates agent-labeled from human-labeled training provenance without accessing the training data.

one_line_idea: Cross-seed disagreement among annotation agents is a cheap detector of genuinely ambiguous instances: agent disagreement predicts human inter-annotator disagreement well enough to route only truly ambiguous items to humans.
core_hypothesis: After controlling for instance difficulty to the agent (via evidence manipulations that fix agent-side failures), residual cross-seed disagreement tracks genuine task ambiguity, correlating with human inter-annotator disagreement strongly enough to serve as a router.
