one_line_idea: Compiling natural-language annotation guidelines into executable checklists (ordered binary probes with evidence requirements) improves agent label consistency more than upgrading the base model, because guideline interpretation is the dominant noise source.
core_hypothesis: Most inter-run label inconsistency traces to unstable guideline interpretation rather than unstable perception; compiling prose into a fixed decision procedure (ordered binary questions, each with an evidence rule) removes the interpretation step and cuts variance more than a model-class upgrade does.

one_line_idea: Given a fixed human budget inside an agent annotation loop, spending it on adjudicating agent disagreements dominates spending it on random spot-checks or gold seeding, and the advantage concentrates exactly where datasets matter most — the ambiguous tail.
core_hypothesis: Human labels are most valuable where agents disagree, because that slice concentrates both agent errors and genuine ambiguity; adjudication allocation therefore yields lower final error than random spot-checking (which mostly audits easy correct labels) or upfront gold seeding (which spends before knowing where help is needed).

one_line_idea: LLM-guided where-to-look policies barely beat brute-force grid scanning at matched crop budgets: most of the reported benefit of visual-search agents comes from having more pixels, not from intelligent search.
core_hypothesis: The dominant term in visual-search gains is resolution recovery (any policy that inspects more pixels wins over a single downscaled pass); the search policy's contribution on top of budget is small except in extreme needle-in-haystack regimes.

one_line_idea: Agent fixations track bottom-up saliency, not the question: look-location distributions barely shift across different questions about the same image, revealing that 'question-guided' viewing in current loops is mostly generic salience.
core_hypothesis: The question's causal effect on look locations is weak: across-question variation in fixation distributions for a fixed image is a small fraction of across-image variation, and the fixations correlate better with generic saliency than with question-relevant ground-truth regions.

one_line_idea: A single forced confirmatory zoom on the claimed evidence region after answering cuts hallucinated-detail errors at negligible cost, because most hallucinations are never re-inspected by the loop.
core_hypothesis: A minimal protocol change — after drafting an answer, the agent must localize its evidence region, zoom into it, and re-affirm or retract — removes the subset of hallucinations that direct re-inspection can falsify, at the cost of one crop encode per answer.

one_line_idea: Loop step order is a first-class variable: agents that draft an answer before zooming anchor on the draft and ignore contradicting crop evidence, while zoom-first ordering avoids the anchor at identical compute.
core_hypothesis: A drafted answer in the transcript acts as an anchor: when subsequent crops contradict it, the agent disproportionately retains the draft; reversing the order (gather crops, then draft) removes the anchor and changes final answers on exactly the contradicted subset.

one_line_idea: Agents cannot judge evidence sufficiency — prompted 'can you answer now?' probes are near chance — but a small stopping head trained on loop traces predicts sufficiency well, converting wasted fixed-depth loops into adaptive ones.
core_hypothesis: Sufficiency information exists in the loop's state (answer stability across recent steps, crop-content statistics) even though verbal self-probes cannot express it; a lightweight trained head on those features predicts whether further looking will change the answer, enabling adaptive stopping.

one_line_idea: Accuracy versus number of accumulated crops is non-monotone: beyond a small working set, added crops interfere with earlier evidence and net accuracy declines, giving each controller a measurable optimal working-set size.
core_hypothesis: There is an interior optimum in working-set size: relevant crops added beyond it displace or interfere with the use of earlier crops, so accuracy rises, peaks, and falls — and the peak location is a stable property of the controller measurable once and reusable as a loop parameter.

one_line_idea: Enumeration loops that mark counted instances repair the systematic undercount of one-shot VLM counting on dense scenes: the fix is loop structure, not model scale, and the crossover density is measurable.
core_hypothesis: Externalizing the counting algorithm — the loop marks each counted instance on the image and re-queries for unmarked ones until none remain — removes the working-memory bottleneck that causes undercounting, with gains growing in scene density while model scale at fixed protocol gains little.

one_line_idea: In multi-view settings, language-reasoned next-view selection adds little over random next views except on the occlusion-limited subset — and that subset is identifiable in advance, telling systems when view planning is worth its cost.
core_hypothesis: View-planning value is concentrated: on most multi-view instances any additional view suffices (or none is needed), so reasoned selection matches random; only where occlusion geometry makes most views uninformative does reasoning pay, and a cheap occlusion probe identifies that subset beforehand.

one_line_idea: Maintaining a persistent low-resolution global view alongside high-resolution foveal crops beats sequences of uniform crops at equal token budget, because zoom loops measurably lose global context — scale and off-crop relations — when the overview is dropped.
core_hypothesis: The failure is architectural, not perceptual: a foveal layout (persistent downscaled overview plus current crop, same total tokens as two crops) preserves the global reference frame, cutting scale and relation errors relative to crops-only loops without any model change — the visual analog of keeping the map while reading the street sign.

one_line_idea: Multi-agent visual debate converges to the shared percept, not the truth: same-backbone debaters agree more and stay wrong on perception errors, with stated confidence rising while accuracy is flat.
core_hypothesis: Debate's value is bounded by percept decorrelation: same-backbone debates on perception-bound errors produce consensus without correction (confidence up, accuracy flat), while mixed-backbone debates recover a real fraction of those errors — making encoder diversity, not debate structure, the active ingredient.

one_line_idea: Vision-agent ensemble gains come from vision-encoder diversity, not LLM diversity: mixing LLMs over a shared encoder yields little, while mixing encoders under one LLM captures most of the full-ensemble gain.
core_hypothesis: Visual errors originate mostly in the encoder, so ensemble decorrelation requires encoder diversity: a 2x2 factorial (encoder same/different x LLM same/different) will show the encoder factor dominating ensemble gain, with LLM diversity contributing marginally on perception-bound tasks.

one_line_idea: Role prompts change transcripts, not outcomes: skeptic/looker/reasoner roles only improve multi-agent vision accuracy when the roles receive different inputs, so engineered information asymmetry — not persona text — is the active ingredient.
core_hypothesis: Functional specialization requires informational specialization: giving the 'skeptic' only the image and the bare claim (not the proposer's reasoning), and the 'looker' only crops (not the question history), creates genuinely decorrelated judgments that persona text alone cannot, converting role-play into measurable division of labor.

one_line_idea: An adversarial checker agent instructed to construct the disconfirming view — the specific crop or transformation that would falsify the claim — beats confirmation-style verification at equal cost, importing falsification-seeking into vision loops.
core_hypothesis: Falsification is an actionable visual strategy: for claims like 'there are three cups' or 'the sign says stop', there exists a specific view (crop, zoom, contrast change) most likely to reveal the claim false if it is; an agent trained by instruction to construct and execute that view detects more errors than one asked to double-check, at the same budget.

one_line_idea: Hallucinated details become sticky in multi-agent transcripts: once an unsupported visual claim is repeated twice, its adoption probability by other agents exceeds its correction probability, quantifying error contagion as a system property.
core_hypothesis: Transcript repetition manufactures credibility: the probability that a downstream agent adopts an unsupported claim rises with each repetition, crossing the probability of correction after about two mentions, so pipelines have a measurable contagion threshold beyond which errors become collectively locked in.

one_line_idea: Splitting dense scenes among parallel agents pays only above a measurable object-density threshold: below it, coordination and double-counting costs exceed parallel gains, and the crossover is predictable from single-agent working-set limits.
core_hypothesis: Partitioned processing helps exactly when single-agent capacity saturates: the crossover density where partitioning starts to win coincides with the single agent's measured working-set limit, making the deployment decision predictable from a cheap single-agent measurement rather than from full system A/B tests.

one_line_idea: Tool-set diversity decorrelates agent errors where temperature and prompt diversity do not: assigning different tool access to ensemble members lowers error correlation and lifts ensemble accuracy beyond any sampling-based diversity at equal cost.
core_hypothesis: Diversity must enter through evidence, not sampling: members with different tool access (one zooms, one reads text, one queries structure) make errors in different places, and measured pairwise error correlation — the quantity that governs ensemble gains — drops substantially only under tool-set diversity.

one_line_idea: In multi-agent vision exchanges, message confidence markers predict claim adoption more than attached image evidence does: agents weigh rhetoric over pixels, making persuasive-but-wrong agents systematically dangerous in mixed pipelines.
core_hypothesis: Adoption of claims by receiving agents is governed more by linguistic confidence than by evidential attachment: in a factorial manipulation (confident/hedged phrasing x evidence attached/absent), the phrasing coefficient will dominate the evidence coefficient, exposing a systematic vulnerability to persuasive error.

one_line_idea: VLM-judge failures decompose into perception failures (cannot see the difference) and criterion failures (sees it, wrong rubric): an oracle-perception protocol — feeding ground-truth descriptions instead of pixels — cleanly splits the two and tells you whether to fix eyes or rubric.
core_hypothesis: Substituting verified textual descriptions of the compared items for the images themselves removes the perception load while preserving the judgment task; the disagreement that disappears under substitution is perception-borne, the remainder is criterion-borne, giving a reusable decomposition instrument for any judging task.

one_line_idea: The generator-verifier gap that powers self-improvement in code and math is absent for perception: judging a visual answer requires the same percept as producing it, so same-model visual judges provide no exploitable training signal.
core_hypothesis: For perception-bound tasks there is no verification shortcut: the judge must re-perform the same perceptual computation as the generator, so same-model judge accuracy tracks generator accuracy instead of exceeding it, and the exploitable gap that drives code/math self-improvement is structurally missing.

one_line_idea: Judges given executable rubrics — per-item binary checks each requiring pointed image evidence — agree with humans more than holistic judges at equal cost, converting judging from perception-plus-taste into a sequence of verifiable micro-perceptions.
core_hypothesis: Decomposing judgment into an executable rubric (does output A mislabel any object? does it miss the requested attribute? — each answered with a pointed region) converts one hard judgment into several easy perceptions, raising human agreement at matched compute and making judge verdicts auditable item by item.

one_line_idea: Visual-judge self-preference is stylistic, not substantive: rewriting identical answer content in another model family's style moves judge preference, showing the bias lives in surface-form recognition rather than content assessment.
core_hypothesis: Self-preference is carried by style: holding answer content fixed (same claims, same regions, same verdicts) while transplanting the surface style of another family will move the judge's preference by nearly as much as swapping actual content producers — localizing the bias to recognizable form.

one_line_idea: Reference-based visual judging penalizes correct-but-different answers: judges overweight surface similarity to the reference, and the penalty on verified-equivalent paraphrases is large enough to flip system rankings that depend on judge scores.
core_hypothesis: Judges given references shift from image-grounded assessment to text-matching: verified-equivalent answers phrased unlike the reference lose points that identical-content reference-like phrasings keep, and the effect size is large enough to reorder systems whose outputs differ in phrasing style.

one_line_idea: VLM judges fail on dense geometric outputs but recover with rendered comparisons: overlaying prediction-vs-reference differences as visual diffs lifts judge accuracy on box and keypoint quality far above judging from raw pairs, mapping a capability boundary and its fix.
core_hypothesis: The failure is presentational: raw side-by-side geometric comparison overloads the judge, but rendering the disagreement itself (color-coded diff overlays marking added/missing/shifted elements) converts the task into perception of highlighted differences, recovering most of the gap to geometric-metric ground truth.

one_line_idea: Using a VLM judge as a training reward has a measurable hacking onset: as optimization pressure grows, policies exploit judge blind spots at a predictable point, and the onset is a property of the judge-policy pair estimable before full training.
core_hypothesis: Hacking onset is systematic: as optimization pressure (divergence from the initial policy) increases, judge score and true quality first rise together, then diverge at a pressure threshold characteristic of the judge-policy pair — and a cheap probe (scoring deliberately style-perturbed outputs to map the judge's blind-spot directions) predicts that threshold without running full training.

one_line_idea: Pairwise visual-judgment intransitivity is a cheap reliability meter: cycle rate in a small tournament predicts judge-human agreement without any human labels, and cycle-repaired rankings recover accuracy the raw judge lacks.
core_hypothesis: Preference cycles (A beats B beats C beats A) are logical inconsistencies whose frequency tracks the judge's noise level: cycle rate measured on a small round-robin correlates with human agreement across judges and tasks, and fitting a consistent global ranking through the cycles yields better orderings than raw pairwise verdicts.

one_line_idea: End-to-end agent success is worse than the product of per-step success rates: shared context couples steps so that errors interact super-multiplicatively, and the negative interaction term grows with chain length.
core_hypothesis: Context coupling makes step failures mutually reinforcing: a marginal early step degrades the context all later steps condition on, so observed end-to-end success falls below the independence prediction by a coupling term that is measurable per pipeline and grows with depth.

one_line_idea: Under mandatory iso-cost accounting — agent loop versus a bigger single model at matched dollars or FLOPs — a substantial share of reported loop gains disappears, exposing the field's default comparison (loop vs same-size single pass) as systematically flattering.
core_hypothesis: A reproducible iso-cost protocol (fixed accounting rules for tokens, encodes, and tool calls; comparison lines at matched spend) will show that a large fraction of loop advantage is purchased compute rather than architectural insight, while identifying the specific loop mechanisms that survive normalization as genuinely efficient.

one_line_idea: Agent loops should be selected on a measured latency-quality frontier: a 'marginal gain per marginal token' index computed from small pilots predicts which loop designs are Pareto-dominated before full evaluation, and typical configurations sit far inside the frontier.
core_hypothesis: The frontier is cheap to estimate: marginal-gain-per-marginal-token indices measured on a few hundred pilot instances for each loop mechanism extrapolate to full-benchmark Pareto ordering, so dominated configurations can be pruned before expensive evaluation — and most published-style defaults will land well inside the frontier they could reach.

one_line_idea: A five-way failure taxonomy — mis-grounding, stale state, tool misuse, premature stop, over-looping — covers the large majority of vision-agent failures across task families, making targeted repairs tractable and transferable.
core_hypothesis: Vision-agent failures concentrate into a small number of loop-level modes that recur across frameworks and tasks; a five-category taxonomy with operational definitions achieves high coverage and inter-labeler agreement, and per-category repairs (state refresh for staleness, stop-head for over-looping) transfer across pipelines because the categories are properties of loops, not of models.

one_line_idea: Naive retry-on-failure raises hallucination rates: retries conditioned on failure context 'try harder' into confabulation, so second attempts are measurably less grounded than first attempts on the same instances.
core_hypothesis: Failure context plus implicit demand for success pushes retries toward lower evidential standards: on instances where the first attempt correctly abstained or hedged, retries manufacture confident unsupported answers, making the retry distribution strictly less grounded than the first-attempt distribution on matched inputs.

one_line_idea: Accumulated tool logs degrade late-loop decisions at fixed information content: verbatim history hurts relative to faithful summaries, contradicting the more-context-is-safer default for agent memory.
core_hypothesis: Holding decision-relevant information constant, verbatim log accumulation lowers late-step decision quality relative to compact faithful summaries: the interference cost of stale tokens exceeds their marginal informational value from mid-loop onward, and the gap widens with step index.

one_line_idea: Run-to-run variance of full vision-agent pipelines has a stable component structure — controller sampling, prompt formatting, tool nondeterminism — and fixing the top component alone yields most of the achievable reproducibility, telling practitioners which knob to freeze first.
core_hypothesis: Pipeline randomness is hierarchically concentrated rather than diffuse: a designed variance-attribution study (toggling one randomness source at a time under replication) will find one component contributing the majority share consistently across tasks, and freezing it captures most of the reproducibility that freezing everything would.

one_line_idea: Controller intelligence is not the bottleneck: a small fine-tuned controller retains most of a frontier-controller system's end-task accuracy inside a fixed vision-agent scaffold, shifting the cost story of deployed vision agents.
core_hypothesis: Within a fixed scaffold, the controller's job (route, sequence, integrate reports) is far simpler than open-ended reasoning: a small model fine-tuned on the frontier controller's decision traces retains most system accuracy, because the scaffold externalizes the hard structure and the vision tools carry the perception.

one_line_idea: Vision tools degrade inside loops because agents feed them off-distribution inputs — extreme crops, odd aspect ratios, resampled regions; measuring the in-loop degradation factor and adding an input-standardization wrapper recovers most of it without touching tools or controller.
core_hypothesis: In-loop tool inputs are measurably off-distribution (size, aspect, context statistics) relative to tool training regimes, causing an in-loop accuracy discount; a standardization wrapper (padding to native aspect, rescaling to native resolution, context-margin retention) restores tool inputs toward distribution and recovers most of the discount — for captioners, detectors, OCR, and promptable segmentation tools alike.

one_line_idea: Independently validated loop enhancements do not stack: pairwise interactions among verification, zooming, and voting are mostly zero or negative, so system builders need interaction-aware selection rather than feature accumulation.
core_hypothesis: Enhancement gains draw from overlapping error pools (each mechanism fixes the easy recoverable subset first) and interact through context (verification transcripts degrade zoom decisions), so the pairwise interaction matrix over standard mechanisms is predominantly non-positive and full stacks underperform the best single or pair configurations at matched compute.

one_line_idea: Log-depth versus metric-depth regression targets act as fixed per-pixel gradient preconditioners, so the log target should win exactly on scenes whose depth-range ratio exceeds a predictable threshold and be irrelevant on shallow-range scenes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The target parameterization acts as a diagonal preconditioner on per-pixel gradients: metric-depth L1 gives far pixels gradient magnitudes proportional to their absolute error scale, so on wide-range scenes far regions dominate the update budget and near-field structure is starved; log-depth equalizes relative-error gradients across the range. The active ingredient is gradient allocation, not representational capacity.

one_line_idea: Angular losses for surface-normal regression have a curvature blow-up near large errors that produces heavy-tailed gradient spikes early in training, and switching the early phase to bounded vector losses removes the spikes and the late-training accuracy debt they cause.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Early in training, a nontrivial fraction of pixels sit at large angular error where the angular loss Jacobian is ill-conditioned; these pixels emit gradient spikes that destabilize shared features, and the damage is done in the first fraction of training when spike frequency is highest.

one_line_idea: Polar (magnitude, angle) parameterization of optical-flow targets is ill-conditioned at small motions because angle gradients diverge as magnitude goes to zero, predicting a specific small-motion accuracy deficit that Cartesian targets do not have.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In polar coordinates the angle target is undefined at zero motion and its gradient scales like 1/magnitude, so pixels with near-zero flow inject high-variance angular gradients; training with polar targets therefore selectively degrades the small-motion regime while matching Cartesian training on large motions.

one_line_idea: Signed-distance-field regression redistributes boundary-concentrated gradients across the whole image plane, and its benefit over per-pixel mask classification is predictable from how concentrated the mask-loss gradient field is (thin, elongated classes benefit; blob classes do not).
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Cross-entropy on masks concentrates useful gradient in a thin band around boundaries once interiors saturate, so classes whose gradient field has high spatial concentration (high Gini coefficient over pixels) train slowly; regressing a signed distance field spreads informative gradient over all pixels and helps exactly those classes, for optimization rather than representational reasons.

one_line_idea: The Gaussian sigma of keypoint heatmap targets is an implicit learning-rate schedule, so annealing sigma during training should dominate any fixed sigma, and two runs ending at the same sigma but with different trajectories should end at measurably different accuracy.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Target sigma controls the spatial support and magnitude of per-pixel gradients around each keypoint, so it functions as a spatial learning-rate and curriculum knob: large sigma early accelerates coarse localization, small sigma late sharpens precision, and the trajectory of sigma matters independently of its final value.

one_line_idea: Classification-over-bins beats direct regression for dense continuous targets mainly because it bounds per-pixel gradient magnitude, so regression with matched per-pixel gradient clipping should erase most of the gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant active ingredient is gradient boundedness: cross-entropy over bins caps the per-pixel gradient regardless of error size, while L1/L2 regression lets outlier pixels dominate updates; on heavy-tailed targets this difference alone explains most of the gap, independent of any multimodality story.

one_line_idea: Softmax versus per-class sigmoid output parameterization in semantic segmentation determines whether co-occurring classes exchange gradients competitively, predicting opposite confusion dynamics for class pairs that frequently share boundaries.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Softmax couples class logits so that every positive update for class A at a pixel is a negative update for class B, creating zero-sum dynamics concentrated at co-occurring class pairs; sigmoid decouples them. Therefore softmax training should show anti-correlated within-run fluctuations of confusable-pair accuracies and faster separation of frequently adjacent classes, while sigmoid should show independent drift and more inter-class leakage at shared boundaries.

one_line_idea: Supervising dense outputs in a frequency-decomposed basis lets one schedule which spatial frequencies are learned when, and this only changes outcomes under truncated training budgets, pinpointing spectral acquisition order as a budget-dependent bottleneck.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Reweighting the loss in a wavelet or Fourier basis directly reallocates gradient across frequency bands, so a high-frequency-boosted schedule can pull forward detail acquisition; because the default ordering resolves itself given enough steps, the intervention's benefit should shrink to zero as budget grows, with a measurable crossover budget.

one_line_idea: Dice loss is an implicit instance-size reweighting schedule whose strength grows as predictions sharpen, predicting that dice beats cross-entropy only when the target size distribution is heavy-tailed beyond a measurable threshold.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dice normalizes each structure's contribution by its predicted+true size, so per-pixel gradients scale inversely with structure size, and this reweighting intensifies during training as soft predictions contract toward the structure; dice-vs-CE outcomes are therefore governed by the tail exponent of the size distribution, not by class imbalance per se.

one_line_idea: Structured surrogate losses like Lovász hinge help exactly when a model's errors are spatially clustered, because their pixel-gradient coupling coordinates updates within an error blob, predicting the gain from a pre-training error-autocorrelation measurement.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] These losses couple gradients across pixels of the same class within an image (through the sorted-error construction), effectively making coordinated blob-level corrections; when errors are spatially independent the coupling adds variance without benefit, so the spatial autocorrelation length of the error field determines the sign of the effect.

one_line_idea: Focal loss is functionally an annealed hard-pixel selection schedule: replacing it with explicit top-k pixel selection whose k follows focal's shrinking effective-support trajectory should reproduce its gains, killing the reweighting-form story.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] What matters is not the weighting form but the induced trajectory of effective support: as the model improves, the fraction of pixels with non-negligible focal gradient shrinks, making focal an automatic anneal from all-pixel to hard-pixel training; any selection scheme matching that support trajectory will match focal.

one_line_idea: Cross-entropy training drives dense-head logit norms to grow roughly logarithmically, imposing a hidden effective-LR decay on decision geometry; norm-controlled heads should therefore need explicit schedule compensation, exposing an unacknowledged coupling between loss and schedule.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Growing logit norms shrink softmax gradients for correctly classified pixels, acting as an implicit per-pixel LR decay concentrated on easy regions; part of what cosine decay 'does' for segmentation is redundant with this implicit decay, so fixing the logit norm (weight-normalized head with fixed temperature) redistributes when and where learning happens and requires a different explicit schedule to match.

one_line_idea: Boundary-region learning is gradient-starved until interiors saturate, making interior-then-boundary acquisition an optimization-forced order; boundary emphasis should therefore only matter under short training budgets, with a predictable crossover.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Early in training, interior pixels dominate the gradient budget because they are numerous and initially wrong; boundary pixels receive meaningful gradient only after interiors saturate. Boundary emphasis merely pulls this phase forward, so its value decays with budget and vanishes when the natural boundary phase completes within the schedule.

one_line_idea: Class-frequency loss reweighting interacts destructively with momentum: rare-class gradient bursts get smeared into subsequent unrelated batches, so reweighting gains should shrink as momentum grows, an interaction nobody tunes for.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Rare classes appear in occasional bursts; amplifying their loss creates large transient gradients that momentum carries into many following steps where the rare class is absent, applying stale rare-class updates against unrelated batches and partially undoing the intended effect; lower momentum or momentum-reset-on-burst should restore the reweighting benefit.

one_line_idea: Whether combining two dense losses helps is determined by the spatial structure of their per-pixel gradient disagreement: structured disagreement (different losses own different pixel populations) yields complementary gains, diffuse disagreement yields averaging.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Two losses help jointly when their per-pixel gradient sign disagreements concentrate on distinct, coherent pixel populations (e.g., one loss dominates boundaries, the other interiors), so each population gets a consistent signal; when disagreement is spatially diffuse the combination merely averages and adds variance.

one_line_idea: Temperature in pixel-level contrastive objectives sets the effective number of negatives that receive gradient, and the right temperature is determined by the intra-class visual diversity of the dataset, predicting opposite tuning directions for homogeneous versus diverse datasets.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Low temperature concentrates gradient on the hardest negatives; in dense settings the hardest negatives for diverse classes are frequently semantically same-class pixels (other instances, distant parts), so low temperature actively teaches wrong invariances on diverse datasets while sharpening useful boundaries on homogeneous ones; the optimal temperature therefore increases with measured intra-class feature diversity.

one_line_idea: Pairwise/structured consistency terms in dense losses act mostly as spatial gradient-noise dampers, so replacing them with content-blind local gradient smoothing should reproduce the bulk of their reported gains.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The operative effect of these terms is variance reduction: they average gradient signals over neighborhoods, damping per-pixel supervision noise; the structural content (affinity correctness) is mostly irrelevant, so content-blind smoothing of the per-pixel gradient field with a matched kernel should recover most of the benefit.

one_line_idea: Asymmetric region losses (Tversky-style) change ranking quality only when class overlap in feature space is itself asymmetric; otherwise they merely slide along the precision-recall curve, which threshold-free ranking metrics will expose.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] If the learned score function's ranking of pixels is unchanged, asymmetry only moves the operating point, which post-hoc threshold selection achieves for free; asymmetry genuinely improves ranking only when the two error types originate from feature-space regions of different learnability, an asymmetry measurable before training.

one_line_idea: Adam's advantage over SGD for transformer-based dense predictors is concentrated in attention-projection layers with heavy-tailed gradient distributions, so adaptive preconditioning applied only to those layers should recover most of the gap at SGD-like memory cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The Adam requirement is localized: attention projections produce per-parameter gradient distributions with much heavier tails than convolutions, and only those layers need adaptive step normalization; the rest of the network trains fine under SGD, so a hybrid optimizer (Adam on attention, SGD elsewhere) matches full Adam.

one_line_idea: Adam's beta2 is a rare-event memory horizon: rare-class gradient bursts decay out of the second-moment estimate between occurrences, so rare-class accuracy should depend on beta2 with a crossover predicted by the class recurrence interval.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For parameters serving rare classes, the second-moment estimate decays toward zero between class occurrences when (1-beta2)^(-1) is shorter than the recurrence interval, producing oversized steps on the next occurrence (or undersized after clipping); matching the beta2 horizon to the class recurrence time should measurably improve rare-class learning.

one_line_idea: Most of weight decay's accuracy effect in fine-tuned dense predictors is mediated by the final head's logit-scale dynamics, so decaying only the head should reproduce full-network decay, contradicting the feature-regularization story.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] In fine-tuning regimes (short schedules, pretrained features), decay's main causal path is controlling head weight growth, which sets logit scale and thus the effective per-pixel gradient decay (cf. the CE logit-growth mechanism); backbone decay is mostly inert at these horizons, so head-only decay is sufficient.

one_line_idea: Global gradient clipping in dense training triggers almost exclusively on a tiny, stable population of image-crop configurations, so it functions as implicit example down-weighting; removing those crops should reproduce clipping's benefit without any clipping.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Clip events are not diffuse: they concentrate on a heavy-tailed set of specific images and crop positions (extreme content, degenerate supervision regions), so clipping's real function is to down-weight a small pathological subpopulation; identifying and excluding (or down-weighting) that subpopulation reproduces the benefit and reveals what the pathology actually is.

one_line_idea: Weight EMA helps dense prediction in proportion to augmentation strength because it averages out augmentation-induced weight oscillations, predicting near-zero EMA gains in weak-augmentation regimes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant noise source EMA averages in modern dense recipes is augmentation-induced gradient variance (strong crops, color jitter, mosaic-style mixing), so the EMA gain is an increasing function of augmentation strength at matched LR, and vanishes when augmentation is weak because remaining minibatch noise is already small at typical batch sizes.

one_line_idea: Layer-wise LR decay and shortened training are two projections of one variable, total feature rotation, so (decay factor, schedule length) pairs producing equal rotation should produce equal dense-task transfer, collapsing a 2D tuning grid to 1D.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Both knobs operate by limiting how far early-layer features rotate away from pretraining; the transfer-relevant state variable is cumulative early-layer rotation (measurable as CKA drift or subspace angle), so configurations matched on final rotation are exchangeable regardless of which knob produced the rotation.

one_line_idea: Sign-based and update-normalized optimizers help dense training only when inter-layer gradient-scale disparity exceeds a threshold, because their active ingredient is per-layer update-norm equalization, which plain SGD plus per-layer normalization reproduces.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] These optimizers' main effect in dense-prediction training is equalizing update magnitudes across layers with wildly different gradient scales (heads vs backbone, early vs late blocks); when a network's layerwise gradient-scale spread is small, they offer nothing, so SGD with explicit per-layer update normalization is an equivalence control that isolates the ingredient.

one_line_idea: Gradient accumulation is not equivalent to large-batch training for dense models with batch normalization, because BN statistics see micro-batches; the folklore equivalence silently breaks and the break size is predictable from BN's batch-size noise curve.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Accumulated micro-batches produce identical summed gradients only for batch-independent layers; BN computes statistics per micro-batch, injecting extra statistic noise and changing the optimization trajectory, so accumulation-vs-true-large-batch differences should scale with BN's statistic variance at the micro-batch size and disappear under GroupNorm.

one_line_idea: The folklore that loss scale does not matter under Adam fails for dense per-pixel-mean losses whose magnitude approaches Adam's epsilon, predicting resolution-dependent silent undertraining and a one-line epsilon fix.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] When typical per-parameter gradient magnitudes fall within an order of magnitude of epsilon, Adam's effective step shrinks nonuniformly (most for small-gradient parameters), which systematically undertrains exactly the low-gradient directions dense models need late in training; the effect strengthens with output resolution under mean reduction and vanishes under sum reduction with rescaled LR.

one_line_idea: The linear batch-size/LR scaling rule breaks earlier for dense tasks than classification because pixels within an image are correlated samples, making the critical batch size a function of intra-image gradient correlation rather than image count.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The relevant noise scale for the scaling rule is set by effective independent sample count; dense-task gradients from pixels of one image are strongly correlated, so the effective sample count is closer to the image count times a task-dependent factor below 1, predicting that dense tasks exit the noise-dominated regime (where linear scaling holds) at systematically smaller batch sizes than classification on matched backbones.

one_line_idea: Warmup in dense fine-tuning primarily protects the randomly initialized head-to-backbone interface, so warming up only the head's learning rate should reproduce full-network warmup and identify whose instability warmup actually fixes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At fine-tuning start, the random head emits large, misdirected gradients into well-conditioned pretrained features; the harmful transient is confined to this interface, so per-module warmup analysis will show head-only warmup suffices, while backbone-only warmup does nothing, reframing warmup as interface protection rather than global stabilization.

one_line_idea: For dense prediction, the tail integral of the LR schedule is a sufficient statistic: cosine, step, and poly schedules matched on late-phase LR integral should produce equal accuracy, reducing schedule-shape debates to one number.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Final dense-task accuracy is dominated by how much low-LR refinement the tail provides (the integral of LR over the last phase, which sets both the final noise floor and the amount of fine-structure consolidation); shape differences elsewhere matter only through this quantity, so schedules matched on tail integral are interchangeable within noise.

one_line_idea: Final learning rate sets a spatial-frequency noise floor: boundary-band accuracy keeps improving as final LR decreases long after interior accuracy saturates, following a power law that tells practitioners when further decay is wasted.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] SGD noise at LR eta prevents consolidation of parameters whose loss curvature is below a threshold proportional to eta; fine spatial structure (boundary bands, thin parts) lives in low-curvature directions, so decreasing final LR extends accuracy specifically in high-frequency regions, with interior/blob accuracy saturating early; the region-resolved accuracy-vs-final-LR curve should follow a power law with region-dependent exponents.

one_line_idea: The last-epochs augmentation-off trick works as a short distribution re-adaptation phase whose required length is set by augmentation strength and normalization-statistics inertia, not by total training length, predicting a fixed small step budget suffices at any scale.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The trick's function is to let the network re-fit clean-data statistics (normalization buffers, low-level feature detectors) after training under a shifted augmented distribution; the required length is governed by the adaptation time constant of those statistics, which depends on augmentation strength and LR at the switch, and is independent of total run length.

one_line_idea: Cyclic-LR snapshot ensembles for dense prediction gain almost entirely at spatial decision boundaries because cycles re-randomize low-curvature boundary placements while interiors are pinned, predicting ensemble gains concentrate in trimap bands.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] After the first convergence, high-curvature directions (interior/semantic decisions) are stable across cycles, while low-curvature directions (exact boundary placement, thin-part extent) get re-sampled each cycle; ensembling therefore averages boundary hypotheses, and its benefit should be predictable from the between-cycle disagreement map, which will concentrate near boundaries.

one_line_idea: Mean-validation-loss early stopping systematically truncates late-acquired classes in dense training because per-class acquisition is staggered, so class-resolved stopping criteria should recover rare-class accuracy that standard practice silently discards.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The mean criterion is dominated by frequent classes that peak (and start overfitting) early, so the selected checkpoint predates rare-class convergence by a margin that grows with acquisition stagger; selecting per-class-optimal checkpoints (or stopping on a stagger-aware criterion) recovers rare-class accuracy at negligible frequent-class cost because their overfitting slope is shallow.

one_line_idea: Warmup length requirements scale inversely with pixels-per-batch, not images-per-batch, because dense gradient noise is set by supervised-pixel count, predicting high-resolution training needs far less warmup than folklore prescribes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The early instability warmup mitigates scales with gradient noise, which for dense losses is governed by total supervised pixels per batch (images x pixels, discounted by intra-image correlation); larger crops at fixed image count therefore reduce required warmup, a dependence invisible to image-count-based folklore.

one_line_idea: The freeze-then-unfreeze fine-tuning ritual creates a measurable gradient shock at the unfreeze step, and gradual unfreezing only helps when that shock exceeds a threshold, giving a one-measurement rule for whether the gentler schedule is worth implementing.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] At unfreeze, the adapted head suddenly backpropagates into unadapted features, producing a gradient-norm spike and transient accuracy dip whose magnitude depends on how far the head specialized during the frozen phase; gradual unfreezing amortizes this shock, so its benefit is a monotone function of measured shock size, near zero below a threshold.

one_line_idea: Constant-LR-plus-EMA matches decayed schedules on interior-dominated metrics but systematically lags on boundary-sensitive metrics, because weight averaging only mimics decay where the local loss is quadratic, which boundary directions violate.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Averaging iterates equals decaying LR only under local quadratic structure; dense boundary directions have non-quadratic, asymmetric loss geometry (small shifts asymmetrically flip pixel sets), so the averaged weights land measurably off the low-LR limit specifically in boundary behavior while matching in interiors, producing a metric-dependent verdict on schedule-free training.

one_line_idea: Strong-augmentation-early, weak-late ordering beats the reverse only under short budgets, because high-LR phases absorb high-variance augmentation gradients while low-LR phases cannot, predicting an ordering-by-budget interaction with a crossover.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Augmentation adds gradient variance that is cheap to absorb when LR-driven noise already dominates (early, high LR) and expensive when the model is consolidating (late, low LR); therefore strong-early/weak-late dominates the reverse ordering, but the margin shrinks as total budget grows because both orderings eventually see enough clean low-LR steps.

one_line_idea: The linear-probe-then-finetune advantage for dense tasks can be earned adaptively: hold the backbone until the head's gradient norm falls below a fixed fraction of the backbone's, then release, matching tuned two-stage recipes without tuning the stage boundary.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The damage two-stage training prevents is caused by large random-head gradients flowing into the backbone; the natural stage boundary is therefore when the head-to-backbone gradient-norm ratio drops below a small constant, and an online rule releasing the backbone at that crossing captures the full benefit across setups with one universal constant.

one_line_idea: Dense fine-tuning proceeds in two intrinsic phases, normalization/bias adaptation first and weight-matrix rotation second, and the first phase alone accounts for most in-domain gain, making the phase boundary a natural budget knob.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Early fine-tuning gains come from re-centering activation statistics (norm/bias), which requires no feature rewriting; weight matrices begin rotating substantially only after this re-centering saturates, and the second phase contributes mainly on classes/structures absent from pretraining, so the phase decomposition predicts which tasks can stop after phase one.

one_line_idea: Forgetting of pretraining abilities during dense fine-tuning is episodic rather than gradual, concentrated in identifiable step windows tied to LR milestones and batch composition, so cheap interventions targeted at those windows should preserve abilities at negligible cost.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Ability loss is not a smooth drift: probe accuracy on pretraining-proxy tasks drops in discrete episodes coinciding with LR increases/milestones and rare-content batches, because forgetting requires large coordinated updates that only those windows provide; guarding only those windows (temporary trust-region or EMA fallback) preserves abilities nearly as well as continuous regularization at a fraction of the interference.

one_line_idea: Head initialization scale bifurcates dense fine-tuning into feature-reuse and feature-rewrite regimes at a sharp threshold, making one init hyperparameter a regime selector that explains bimodal fine-tuning outcomes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Small-gain heads produce small early gradients, keeping the backbone near its pretrained function (lazy/reuse regime); large-gain heads inject gradients that push the backbone out of the pretrained basin within the first hundreds of steps (rich/rewrite regime); the transition is sharp in init gain and its location is roughly predictable from first-step gradient-norm ratios.

one_line_idea: The weight-update matrices of full dense-task fine-tuning have systematically higher effective rank than classification fine-tuning on matched backbones, quantifying why low-rank adaptation recipes ported from classification underfit dense tasks.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The intrinsic dimensionality of the required weight change is a task property: dense prediction requires spatially diverse feature edits (many independent directions across scales and positions), so the effective rank (participation ratio of singular values) of full fine-tuning deltas will be several-fold higher for dense tasks than classification on the same backbone, concentrated in spatial-mixing layers.

one_line_idea: Dense fine-tuning exits the linearly-connected basin of its initialization within a few hundred steps while classification fine-tuning stays connected for most of training, giving a sharp geometric signature of how much dense adaptation restructures solutions.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense objectives reshape spatial-mixing computations enough that the fine-tuned solution leaves the init-connected basin early, whereas classification fine-tuning famously stays connected; the exit time (first step whose interpolation to init shows a barrier) is therefore a task-complexity signature, earlier for dense tasks and earlier still for structurally novel target types.

one_line_idea: Intermediate-task fine-tuning helps dense targets mostly by delivering a well-conditioned head and normalization state rather than better features, so transplanting only those components from the intermediate model should reproduce most of the stepping-stone gain.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For dense targets, much of the stepping-stone benefit is optimization-mechanical: the intermediate stage leaves behind an adapted head geometry and normalization statistics that condition the final fine-tune (no random-head shock, statistics already in-range), so transplanting head+norm parameters onto the ORIGINAL backbone recovers most of the gain without any intermediate-feature content.

one_line_idea: The depth of the early-fine-tuning accuracy dip carries no information about final dense-task quality, debunking the practice of culling fine-tuning runs by their first-epochs behavior.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dip depth is governed by interface variables (head init, warmup, first-batch composition) that are nearly independent of the variables governing final quality (data fit, capacity, schedule tail), so early-dip-based run selection is close to random selection and silently discards good configurations.

one_line_idea: The folklore 10x head-LR multiplier is a proxy for equalizing head and backbone adaptation timescales, so the optimal multiplier should collapse toward 1 as head initialization quality improves, unifying two separate fine-tuning rituals.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The multiplier compensates for the head starting at random while the backbone starts converged: it approximately equalizes the two modules' time-to-adaptation. If the head is pre-adapted (probe-initialized), the compensation is unnecessary, so the optimal multiplier is a decreasing function of head-init quality, approaching 1 for fully probed heads; the 10x constant is thus a special case of one underlying variable (initial adaptation asymmetry).

one_line_idea: Re-initializing the final backbone block before dense fine-tuning helps precisely when the pretraining objective's terminal computations conflict with dense decoding, a conflict measurable as high initial gradient opposition in that block.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Late pretrained blocks encode objective-specific terminal computations (e.g., global pooling preparation) that dense decoding must actively undo; when the angle between early fine-tuning gradients and the pretrained block's function is strongly opposed, resetting the block removes an obstacle, while for aligned setups resetting destroys useful structure. The measured initial gradient-opposition score in the final block therefore predicts the sign of the reset effect.

one_line_idea: Frequency-resolved error curves of dense predictors collapse onto one universal acquisition trajectory when time is reparameterized by integrated learning rate, making spectral acquisition order a schedule-invariant law rather than an architecture story.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The controlling clock for spectral acquisition is accumulated effective step size (the integral of LR over steps), not raw steps or epochs; after this reparameterization, frequency-band error trajectories from different schedules and reasonable architecture variants collapse onto one curve, because band ordering is set by loss-surface curvature per band, which the LR integral traverses at schedule-independent order.

one_line_idea: Dense models acquire texture-based discrimination before shape integration within a single training run, and stronger appearance augmentation delays the crossover rather than removing it, making cue reliance a scheduled phase rather than a fixed property.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Texture statistics are learnable by local filters early (low effective receptive field), while shape integration requires long-range assembly that matures later; within-run cue-conflict probing will therefore show a texture-dominant early phase and a partial shift toward shape whose onset scales with effective receptive field growth, with appearance augmentation delaying (not preventing) the texture phase by suppressing early texture reliability.

one_line_idea: Within-class appearance variance, not class frequency, is the dominant determinant of when a class is acquired during segmentation training, inverting the standard imbalance-centric account of late learners.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Acquisition time is governed by how many distinct appearance modes a class spans (its within-class feature variance): a rare but visually homogeneous class is learned quickly, while a frequent but heterogeneous class lags; frequency matters only through exposure count per appearance mode, so variance-per-exposure is the real clock.

one_line_idea: Delayed generalization (grokking-like) exists in dense prediction: under strong weight decay and small data, validation boundary quality jumps long after training loss saturates, with the delay controlled by the decay strength.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Dense tasks have instance-idiosyncratic fit components (exact boundary placements on small training sets) and generalizable components (region semantics); with small data and strong decay, networks first fit boundaries idiosyncratically, then slowly consolidate to transferable boundary rules under the decay pressure, producing a late jump in validation boundary metrics while interior metrics track training loss conventionally.

one_line_idea: Early training at low resolution creates a persistent thin-structure deficit that equal-compute high-resolution fine-tuning cannot repair, establishing a within-run critical period for spatial detail.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Filters and attention patterns that resolve thin structures must form while gradients from those structures exist; at low resolution thin structures vanish from supervision, and the network commits capacity to coarse solutions that later high-resolution gradients only locally patch rather than restructure, leaving a permanent deficit relative to full-resolution-throughout training at matched total compute.

one_line_idea: Detection training acquires localization before classification in a fixed order (matched-box quality saturates while class accuracy still climbs), and the lag between the two phases predicts which errors dominate the final model.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Localization is supervised by geometrically smooth, high-signal regression gradients and matures early; classification of matched boxes requires finer feature discrimination and matures later; the phase lag is architecture- and data-dependent, and a long lag at the end of training (classification still climbing at budget exhaustion) manifests directly as a classification-dominated final error profile.

one_line_idea: Attention-map organization in ViT-based dense models undergoes an abrupt within-run transition (entropy drop plus locality emergence), and dense-task transferability of the features begins rising only after this transition, making it a measurable readiness marker.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Attention organization is a phase transition rather than gradual drift: token-attention entropy drops sharply within a narrow step window as heads differentiate, and until this reorganization happens the features are poorly transferable to dense readouts; the transition time therefore separates an unproductive warm phase from a productive representation phase, and interventions that accelerate the transition (locality-biased init) shift the whole accuracy curve forward.

one_line_idea: Class acquisition order in dense training is optimization-forced, not data-forced: aggressive class-balanced resampling shifts acquisition times but preserves the order, exposing a fixed difficulty hierarchy that data curricula cannot reorder.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Acquisition order reflects intrinsic optimization difficulty (feature depth required, gradient signal geometry) rather than exposure statistics; resampling changes each class's clock speed but not the sequence, so even extreme rebalancing will fail to move early learners behind late learners, bounding what any within-run data curriculum can achieve.

one_line_idea: Epoch-wise double descent in dense prediction is spatially localized: boundary-band validation error is non-monotone over training while interior error descends monotonically, so the phenomenon's visibility depends on which metric a paper reports.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The idiosyncratic-fit-then-consolidation dynamics that produce epoch-wise double descent operate on the hardest, most idiosyncratic pixels, which concentrate near boundaries; interiors are learned smoothly. Dense double descent therefore exists but hides inside spatially aggregated metrics, explaining why it is rarely reported for segmentation.

one_line_idea: Within-run neural collapse in segmentation heads is class-asymmetric: frequent-class features collapse toward their class means early while rare-class features never fully collapse, and the residual within-class variance identifies which classes still benefit from continued training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Collapse progress per class is set by effective gradient exposure, so dense heads exhibit a moving frontier: frequent classes reach near-collapse early (after which their accuracy is optimizer-noise-bound), rare classes remain far from collapse at budget end (data/exposure-bound); the per-class collapse gap therefore partitions classes into those that longer training can still help and those needing other interventions.

one_line_idea: In joint segmentation+depth training, destructive gradient conflict is confined to the top decoder layers, so splitting only those layers should recover nearly all of the fully-split architecture's benefit, replacing task-architecture folklore with a conflict-localization rule.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Task conflict between dense tasks is not uniform across depth: early features (edges, geometry primitives) serve both tasks with aligned gradients, while late decoder layers specialize task-specifically; measured per-layer conflict will show a sharp rise near the top, and architecture splits placed at the measured conflict onset will capture the full-split benefit with minimal parameter cost.

one_line_idea: Deep-supervision auxiliary heads work as per-depth gradient-norm equalizers, so removing them and directly rescaling per-block learning rates to match their induced gradient profile should reproduce their accuracy, collapsing an architectural ritual into an optimizer setting.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The operative effect of auxiliary heads is to raise effective gradient magnitude at earlier blocks, compensating depth attenuation; the representational content of the auxiliary task is largely irrelevant, so per-block LR rescaling matched to the measured with-aux gradient-norm profile will reproduce the benefit without any auxiliary computation.

one_line_idea: Optimal task weights in multi-task dense training are those that equalize per-task gradient noise-to-signal ratios measured mid-run, replacing grid search over weights with a two-measurement rule.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Late training is noise-floor-limited: the task whose gradient noise dominates the shared parameters sets everyone's plateau, so the weight vector that equalizes per-task noise-to-signal ratios (gradient variance over squared mean, measured on shared parameters mid-run) coincides with the grid-search optimum; existing schemes work exactly when they approximate this equalization.

one_line_idea: Cross-view consistency gradients in augmentation-consistency training act as beneficial exploration noise early and harmful drag late, predicting that the standard constant or ramp-up consistency weight is backwards at the end of training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Disagreement between views carries two components: informative invariance signal and augmentation-artifact noise; early, both push features usefully (exploration plus invariance), but late in training the artifact component dominates residual disagreement (real invariances are already learned), so consistency gradients increasingly conflict with the supervised signal at low LR, and decaying the consistency weight in the last phase should beat both constant and ramp schedules.

one_line_idea: Confusable class pairs in segmentation exhibit zero-sum oscillation during training, with epoch-to-epoch accuracy fluctuations that are anti-correlated pairwise, revealing that late training redistributes a fixed decision boundary rather than improving both classes.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] For a confusable pair, the shared feature evidence is nearly fixed late in training, so gradient updates that help one class necessarily push the shared decision boundary against the other; late-phase per-class fluctuations for such pairs will be strongly anti-correlated (unlike unrelated pairs), and the anti-correlation magnitude identifies which confusions are boundary-redistribution problems (needing feature enrichment) versus under-training problems (fixable by more steps).

one_line_idea: The classification and box-regression branches of dense detectors conflict on shared features with a characteristic time signature (regression gradients shrink as boxes converge while classification persists), explaining mechanistically why decoupled-head designs win and when they stop mattering.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Early in training both branches need coarse localization features and their gradients align; as boxes converge, regression gradients shrink and rotate toward high-frequency refinement directions while classification gradients keep demanding invariant semantic features, so branch conflict on shared features grows over training; the benefit of decoupling therefore accrues late, scales with the measured late-phase conflict, and disappears for short schedules.

one_line_idea: In panoptic training, stuff-region gradients numerically dominate thing-region gradients through sheer pixel count, suppressing instance-discrimination learning; branch-specific batch composition (alternating thing-rich and stuff-rich crops) should fix this without any loss reweighting.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The lag is partly a gradient-budget artifact: stuff regions contribute most supervised pixels per batch, so shared features drift toward stuff-optimal statistics between sparse thing-gradient events; composing batches to alternate thing-dense and stuff-dense crops concentrates thing gradients into coherent updates (less inter-batch dilution), improving thing performance at equal data and loss settings.

one_line_idea: Teacher-student dense self-distillation has a two-phase structure with a measurable phase boundary: before teacher-student agreement crosses a threshold the teacher acts as a denoiser, after it the loop locks in student errors, so distillation weight should be scheduled against measured agreement, not time.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] While teacher-student disagreement is high, teacher targets carry independent-enough information to denoise the student; once agreement exceeds a threshold, the residual teacher signal is dominated by the student's own systematic errors reflected back, and continued distillation pressure entrenches them; the transition is detectable online as the point where teacher-corrections stop correlating with ground-truth error reduction on a small labeled probe.

one_line_idea: Cut-and-paste mixing augmentations shift a large share of the boundary-gradient budget onto artificial paste boundaries, so their net effect flips sign between interior-dominated and boundary-sensitive evaluation, resolving contradictory reports about their value for segmentation.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Pasted edges are high-loss, high-gradient regions that compete directly with true-boundary learning for the boundary-gradient budget; the augmentation therefore helps interior/context robustness while systematically taxing true-boundary precision, and the net effect on any benchmark is predicted by the benchmark metric's boundary sensitivity.

one_line_idea: Frozen-BN folklore in detection fine-tuning works because small-batch BN statistic noise acts as an uncontrolled multiplicative perturbation on all downstream computation, so noise-corrected BN (larger virtual batches) should erase the freezing advantage and flip the recommendation at scale.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The harm from live BN at small batches is statistic noise (batch mean/variance estimates jitter), which multiplies activations and destabilizes fine-tuning atop converged features; the harm is therefore a monotone function of statistic noise, so live BN with synchronized or accumulated statistics (large virtual batch) should match or beat frozen BN, and frozen BN should actively hurt when data statistics differ from pretraining.

one_line_idea: BN running-statistics momentum is an implicit schedule that should be tied to the LR schedule: as LR decays, statistics lag the (now slowly moving) weights less, so the fixed default momentum over-smooths late training and under-smooths early training, and matching the two schedules removes a persistent train-eval gap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The optimal statistics-averaging window depends on how fast the underlying activations drift, which is set by the LR schedule; a fixed momentum is therefore wrong twice (too long a memory early when activations move fast, too short late when they are nearly static and noise dominates), and scheduling BN momentum proportionally to LR aligns the estimator with the drift rate, shrinking the train-eval gap and its jitter.

one_line_idea: The BN-vs-GN choice for dense training is governed by a two-dimensional phase boundary in (images per batch, pixels per image): BN wins only above a critical image count that itself grows with resolution, giving a chartable decision diagram instead of contradictory folklore.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] BN's statistic quality depends on effective sample diversity per batch, which for dense features is driven by image count (pixels within an image are correlated and add little), while GN's cost is discarding cross-image statistics; therefore the BN-GN crossover sits at an image-count threshold that is nearly independent of pixel count, predicting BN's regime shrinks at high resolution where memory forces low image counts, and the whole plane is chartable with a modest grid.

one_line_idea: fp16 training with loss scaling loses rare-class gradient contributions first, because their sparse, small-magnitude gradients sit closest to the underflow boundary, creating a class-selective precision tax that fp32 and bf16 do not share.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Underflow in fp16 gradients is not class-neutral: rare classes contribute gradients that are both sparse and small (few pixels, often small structures), so a disproportionate fraction of their gradient mass falls below representable magnitude even with global loss scaling (which is set by the largest gradients); the resulting deficit is invisible in mIoU but measurable in rare-class IoU and in the fraction of underflowed gradient mass per class.

one_line_idea: Multi-resolution dense training works smoothly for LayerNorm architectures but silently degrades BN-based hybrids, because BN statistics are resolution-dependent while LN normalizes per token, predicting a normalization-conditioned verdict on variable-resolution schedules.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Activation statistics at BN layers shift with input resolution (feature-map spatial statistics change with scale), so a batch mixing resolutions or a schedule alternating them forces BN running statistics to track a moving mixture, degrading both training stability and eval-time statistics fidelity; LN-family normalization is per-sample and scale-robust, so transformer-style models tolerate the same schedules, explaining anecdotal architecture-dependent reports about multi-scale training.

one_line_idea: BN's train-mode stochasticity is a load-bearing regularizer in dense training: reproducing its measured noise distribution via explicit activation-noise injection under fixed statistics should recover most of BN's generalization advantage over deterministic normalization.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Batch-statistic jitter perturbs every activation multiplicatively each step, a structured noise correlated within channels and batches; this noise regularizes like a channel-coherent dropout variant, and its contribution can be isolated by freezing statistics (removing estimation) while injecting noise matched to the measured jitter distribution, decomposing BN into estimator + regularizer.

one_line_idea: In normalization-free dense training, adaptive gradient clipping thresholds map onto an equivalent BN batch-size curve, unifying two stability mechanisms as one effective constraint on relative update size and predicting threshold transfer across tasks without tuning.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Both BN and adaptive clipping ultimately bound the relative change a step can impose on a unit's computed function; if so, there is a mapping between clipping threshold and effective BN batch size that equalizes a measurable stability statistic (per-unit relative function change per step), and thresholds chosen by matching that statistic on a new dense task will be near-optimal without task-specific sweeps.

one_line_idea: bf16 and fp16 dense training differ mainly through loss-scaling dynamics rather than representational precision: fp16 with an oracle (perfect, non-adaptive) loss scale should match bf16, isolating the real cost of fp16 as scale-controller misbehavior during gradient-magnitude transients.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] fp16's mantissa is adequate for dense-vision gradients; its failures arise when the dynamic scaling controller reacts to gradient-magnitude transients (schedule changes, hard batches) with scale reductions that then underflow small gradients for thousands of steps; with a fixed oracle scale chosen post-hoc, fp16 matches bf16, implying the fix is controller design, not format switching, where bf16 hardware is unavailable.

one_line_idea: Online hard-example mining is a feedback dynamical system with two regimes: a stable regime where the mined set evolves slowly and mining helps, and a limit-cycle regime where the mined set flips between populations and mining underperforms plain training, with the regime identifiable online from mined-set overlap.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Mining couples model state to data selection: training on mined pixels lowers their loss, ejecting them from the mined set and re-admitting previously easy pixels whose loss rose from neglect; depending on mining ratio and LR this feedback settles (stable frontier) or oscillates (populations alternate); consecutive-epoch mined-set Jaccard overlap distinguishes the regimes, predicting mining's benefit sign without waiting for final metrics.

one_line_idea: The crop-size folklore for segmentation decomposes into a normalization-statistics component and a context component, and controlled statistic-swapping shows which one carries the large-crop advantage, with opposite architectural implications.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] A substantial share of the large-crop advantage flows through normalization statistics (larger crops give more stable per-batch activation statistics at fixed image count), not through longer-range context reaching the loss; swapping statistics across crop regimes (computing BN statistics from large crops while supervising small ones, and vice versa) will attribute the advantage between the two channels, and the context share will concentrate on large-object classes only.

one_line_idea: Per-pixel loss computation is massively redundant: the safe pixel-subsampling rate for loss evaluation is set by the spatial correlation length of the gradient field, giving a measurable dial that trades compute for nothing until a sharp knee.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Neighboring pixels contribute nearly identical gradients through shared receptive fields, so the information content of the per-pixel loss field is governed by its spatial correlation length; random sampling at spacing below that length loses nothing (gradient estimator variance barely rises), while sampling beyond it degrades sharply, producing a knee whose location is predictable from a one-epoch correlation measurement and which shifts with architecture (larger receptive fields tolerate sparser sampling).

one_line_idea: At fixed pixels-per-batch, spending the budget on more images with smaller crops beats fewer images with larger crops for gradient-noise reasons, except where context genuinely binds, giving a decomposable rule for the most common memory tradeoff in dense training.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Gradient estimator variance is dominated by between-image variation, so image count reduces noise roughly linearly while crop growth beyond the network's effective receptive field adds little signal; therefore the many-small configuration wins on optimization grounds, with exceptions confined to classes whose decisive evidence exceeds the crop size (large structures), producing a class-resolved crossover rather than a global winner.

one_line_idea: Within-epoch presentation order leaves a measurable recency imprint on dense models at high learning rates: images seen late in the final epoch are predicted better than statistically identical images seen early, quantifying an ordering bias no one controls for.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Each step moves weights; at high LR the last portion of an epoch overwrites earlier micro-adaptations before any revisit, so a per-image benefit accrues to late positions, decaying with the LR at which the epoch was traversed; the effect concentrates on idiosyncratic image content (rare appearances) and vanishes as LR decays, making final-epoch order a small but systematic bias on per-image and per-rare-class results.

one_line_idea: Gradients from overlapping random crops of the same image are correlated almost linearly in their overlap area, so standard crop samplers waste batch slots; overlap-aware crop sampling recovers the wasted effective batch size for free.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Two crops sharing area produce gradient contributions whose correlation grows near-linearly with overlap fraction (shared receptive fields dominate), so expected effective sample count per batch is computable from the sampler's overlap distribution; a max-coverage/min-overlap sampler at identical cost raises effective batch size and should reproduce the accuracy of a measurably larger standard batch.

one_line_idea: Dense contrastive pretraining with within-image negatives learns positional shortcuts (discriminating by location rather than content), a failure mode absent with cross-image negatives, detectable by a position-decoding probe and fixable by position-debiased sampling.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Within-image negatives are separable by positional cues alone (feature maps carry position through padding and learned biases), so the objective can be satisfied by position-encoding rather than content-encoding features; this shortcut leaves a signature (high position-decoding accuracy from features, weak content transfer), grows with training length, and disappears when negatives come from other images where position is uninformative.
